Recorded verbatim from the critic's hand-back, 2026-10-09. It is model output, not the owner's words. Commissioned by the owner in this session; it overrides, for this plan only, the 2026-08-19 rule that bars critiques of plans (CLAUDE.md rule 0). Orchestrator's spot-checks are appended at the end.

## A. VERDICT

Plan v1 does not satisfy the owner's requirements as drawn: it harvests names, not figures, before it renders; it leaves every slug coupling that matters (search, coverage, mining, candidates, determination record) untouched; and it mass-promotes into a vocabulary with no retire, merge, rename or un-decline path. Per requirement — (1) pipeline quality/logic/sequencing/gates: **FAIL** (Release 0 depends on extractions no phase before render writes; P1/P2 cannot ship as separate PRs under the blocking DoD). (2) Slug-independent scraping: **PARTIAL** (extraction keys on parameter and tolerates cross-slug reads — verified in code — but coverage, candidates, mining and the 2026-09-28 exhaustion ruling are per slug and no slug→parameter mapping exists). (3) Multi-term harvest per source: **FAIL** (one observation per phrase per source; no scan ledger; the quote check the plan cites for observations does not exist). (4) Expandable catalogue: **FAIL** (every expansion path that changes an existing row is a compensating migration).

## B. FINDINGS (worst first)

**F1 · BLOCKER · sequencing/logic.** Claim: B2 "Release 0 ... shows ... which jurisdictions' codes set a requirement ... the evidence state of each parameter"; P2 "mint terms; promote parameters"; P6 "Ongoing: ... scans every source for all parameters". Evidence: no phase before P5 (render) calls `add-extraction`; code attributions and evidence state are derived from `source_value_extractions`, which holds `[(3, 101)]` by parameter [VERIFIED: query]. R16 cannot go red on this — its own PASS text: "whether a parameter goes on to carry an extraction is not read either" (`scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py:964-966`). Failure: P5 renders ten names with no code content; this is GAP-061's shape (harvest, promote, never extract) relabelled as a release. Acceptance: before P5, every catalogued parameter carries ≥1 `claim` row from ≥1 admitted T4–6 source, and a registered check goes red when a catalogued parameter has 0 extractions.

**F2 · BLOCKER · sequencing/gate.** Claim: P1 (research PR, "normal batch gate") then P2 (research PR, "R16, test_db_integrity, review"); "P1 and P2 can overlap by source". Evidence: `research_dod_session` is BLOCKING on `LATEST-RESEARCH` (`governance/check-registry.yaml:1332-1346`); R11-harvest fails any admission with no `observed_terms` row, R16-adjudicate fails any unadjudicated observation, R16 fails any named term undisposed — all scoped to the batch's admissions (`research_batch_dod.py:885-1002`). A P2-only session has 0 admissions → R1, R9a, R9b FAIL "NOTHING IN SCOPE" (`:748, :782`) and R16 prints "EXAMINED: 0 ... asserts nothing". Failure: P1's 40–76 admissions cannot merge COMPLIANT without P2's work in the same stem; P2 alone cannot be gated at all. The plan names no gating stem for P2. Acceptance: one stem per acquisition cohort; harvest+adjudication+disposition ship with the admissions; the record names the stem and every R16 line shows EXAMINED > 0.

**F3 · BLOCKER · multi-term/read-write.** Claim (owner requirement): "harvesting across multiple terms if a source discusses multiple terms". Evidence: `observed_terms UNIQUE (ref_id, surface_form, language)`; `observe_term` returns the prior row with `created: False` (`scripts/db.py:5984-5990`); one adjudication names one `term_id`. Failure: ADA 2010 uses "clear width" at §404.2.3 (door) and §403.5.1 (route); the second sighting is silently folded into the first, its locator and context_quote dropped, the second parameter never named, and R16 sees nothing. Acceptance: a scan of a source where one surface form names two parameters yields two disposed terms and two extractions with distinct locators, and a query shows it.

**F4 · HIGH · slug-independence/conditional.** Claim: P6 "each slug's research scans every source for all parameters"; "Slugs guide our searches, but they do not guide what we derive". What the code does: extraction requires `--slug` (`db.py:1923`) and refuses unless `source_slug_links` holds (ref, slug) (`db.py:7589-7603`); it does NOT check parameter↔slug — J01 was retired for exactly that reason (`scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py:1169-1175`). So ADA §703 tactile height admitted under `accessible-circulation-geometry` extracts under that slug for any active parameter without a slug fiction or a new link — **this half survived**. What does not: `search_executions.slug NOT NULL`, `search_candidates.found_under_slug NOT NULL`, `citation_mining PK (slug, local_ref_id)` (GAP-011), `v_coverage_jurisdiction GROUP BY slug, jurisdiction`, `assess_cell --slug required=True` (`scripts/assess/assess_cell.py:1811`). The 2026-09-28 ruling requires exhaustion "against the slug's parameters" and no table maps slug to parameter [VERIFIED: `sqlite_master` DDL; `slugs.serves_axes` holds 1 row]. The owner's live answer in this session — cross-slug pulls "should be yes, but we still tag it for follow up later" — has no column; only free-text `notes`. Acceptance: a parameter×jurisdiction coverage derivation that reads searches and extractions regardless of slug; a typed cross-slug/follow-up marker a check reads; `assess_cell` no longer demands a slug for a parameter no slug concerns.

**F5 · HIGH · expansion/irreversibility.** Claim: B6 "Promote conservatively; add a retire verb in P3 if needed". Evidence: no retire/merge/rename verb for a parameter (`insert_parameter` docstring `db.py:6362-6367`; grep finds none); `base_parameters.status` admits `merged`/`retired` with no writer (checker without writer, CLAUDE.md §8); no un-decline (`:6456`); `_AMENDABLE_TERM_FIELDS = ("definition", "scope_note")` (`:5245`) so `canonical_en` and `domain` are frozen; direction is write-once (`:6549-6556`); no amend on `observed_terms`. Failure cases the brief asked for: a term that is two parameters, two that are one, a wrong name, a disputed direction — each needs a DR plus compensating migration; at 100 terms that is the whole budget. Sequencing makes it worse: P2's mass promotion precedes P3's "if needed" verb. Acceptance: retire/merge (sweeping extraction pointers) and a provenance-carrying name correction exist, refuse canonical, and are captured by `emit_batch_sql`, before P2 writes at scale.

**F6 · HIGH · logic (D2/D3/D4).** Claim: B5 "Every parameter has exactly one element, or is listed as unassigned"; D3 "One item per element with at least one parameter"; D4 "computed from `terms.domain`". Evidence on the live ten: operating force (door hardware, taps, controls), LRV contrast (surfaces, signage, nosings), reverberation time (a room, no element), colour temperature, headroom clearance, turning circle — none has exactly one element. "Unassigned" makes the leak green and D3 drops every element-less parameter from the catalogue. `terms.domain` is session-typed free text with no CHECK (DDL) and no amend path: D4 "computes" from a curated column (rule 8). Acceptance: parameter→element is N:M; a check goes red when an active parameter reaches no catalogue surface; category source is a CHECK'd vocabulary.

**F7 · HIGH · gate/quality (D1).** Claim: D1 "quote checked against the text by script"; P2 "script checks every quote". Evidence: `_require_verbatim` has one call site, `add-extraction` (`db.py:7676`); `observe_term` and `insert_term` verify nothing. Building it is tooling (rule 10) that a research-labelled P2 cannot carry. Scoping is weak anyway: 11 of 53 sources match artefacts only by URL and 4 (REF-00990, -00991, -00999, -01000) have no artefact at all [VERIFIED: manifests]; GAP-012 leaves pre-2026-09-13 artefacts without `ref_id`, so `quote_in_artefacts` returns UNSCOPED hits (`scripts/research/retrieval_log.py:783-787`). Acceptance: a registered check fails an `observed_terms.context_quote` absent from an artefact persisted for that `ref_id`, reports UNSCOPED separately, and is merged before P2 starts.

**F8 · HIGH · fact/fidelity (A4).** Claim: "A skimmed (preliminary) figure may set a published value if tagged for follow-up — Provisional reading"; "Option A ... Cannot be done by invention; superseded by the next line". Evidence (`transcripts/harness_db856d85/main.jsonl`): the question was "Does a `preliminary` or `skim` extraction ever govern a published cell?"; the owner answered "..yes? like, one pulled from another slug? should be yes, but we still tag it for follow up later" — a ruling about cross-slug extraction, not skim grade. "A" answered "What did you mean by the 90+ cleaned parameters without values?" (A = turn each object into its quantity and propose names for review); "pull from the major codes..." answered a different question (which sources). Failure: B7.6 proposes ledgering these "using your words"; the words recorded would be the session's. Acceptance: each ledger entry quotes the owner verbatim beside the question it answered; the cross-slug ruling is recorded; A's status is put back to the owner.

**F9 · HIGH · fact (Part A).** "Full text is saved for only 14 of the 53 sources (batch 23's)": 49 of 53 have persisted artefacts (38 by ref_id, 11 by URL), ≥6 earlier sources hold PDFs [VERIFIED]. Batch 23's own 14 are partial beyond the three named: DL 163/2006 5/20 pp, Stb 2024/368 4/39, BFS 2024:12 3/9 [VERIFIED: `grep -c '^\[PDF page'`]. "The other sources would be fetched again" contradicts the 2026-09-25 ruling cited one line later. "53 admitted" includes 1 tombstone. A3 omits `source_locators` — 893 rows, 313 with `standard_number`, 880 REFERENCE-ONLY — the largest lead list and R9a/R9b's comparator. The worklist double-counts ≥9 standards (AS 1428.1, CAN/ASC 2.8, DIN 18040-1/-2, EN 17210, ICC A117.1, NEN 9120, PAS 6463, AD M) and lists four blank Co-2 entries. Verified correct: 94/10/17; 191/147/110/49/19; 53 = 11(7+4)/2/11(6+5)/29; 47/6; 101/54; 5; 8 retired, 0 live; 17/17/5 families/17/72/18; 96; 111 (112 with template); 76 = 41 B1 + 19 B2 + 16 INT; 249/25/15; 863.

**F10 · HIGH · gate (B5 vacuity).** Check 5 "Every parameter name traces to an observation with a quoted phrase" is red today on 8 of 10 live parameters (TERM-002/003/005/007/011/021/024/061: 0 adjudications; `data_20261009055057` notes "no source adjudication behind it") and the plan does not say so. Checks 1, 2, 4, 6 have no subject until P3's tables exist → NOTHING-IN-SCOPE on first run. Check 3 duplicates `validate_parameters` (advisory). Acceptance: each B5 check named with EXAMINED subject, level, and the row that fails it today.

**F11 · HIGH · gate/rule 2/9/10.** Claim: P2 "you review the table before anything is written". Evidence: nine `base_parameters` rows are on canonical via `a8b7c11`, committed `[skip ci]`, no PR, no `sessions/` record, no attestation; `adversarial_pass_recorded` (CURRENT) sees `base_parameters` outside limb (a) → NOTHING-IN-SCOPE, green. All nine carry `accessibility_direction NULL`; the engine's most-accommodating rule needs it and the setter is write-once. Acceptance: the rows reach main only via a PR with CI, a record and attestation; owner review recorded before further promotion.

**F12 · MEDIUM · gate (P1 passes with no search — true, and that is the hole).** `add-source` needs no exec or candidate; two live sources have no `search_admissions` edge and no check flags it [VERIFIED]; R9a/R9b pass once admissions carry URLs; RC1 examines only candidates with `surfaced_in` (34 today); `search_log_completeness` is advisory. So a lead-list batch reads COMPLIANT with zero `search_executions` rows — and `v_coverage_jurisdiction`, the 2026-09-28 ruling's only mechanism, records nothing. `origin='lead-index'` exists for this and the plan never uses it. Also owed per admission and unmentioned: R13 population-match row (codes = PROXY), C04 no-DOI explanation (batch 23 hit it), R2/mining rows for every T1–3 advocacy admission, R1 satisfied silently by one Co-1 admission. Acceptance: every lead-list acquisition logged `origin lead-index` under a named slug before admission; a check red when an admitted source has no admission edge.

**F13 · MEDIUM · expansion (new parameter after sources scanned).** No ledger of source×parameter scanned. R16 is per-batch; subject 4 samples once per source per pass; `claim_type='absent'` is the only "scanned, nothing" record (3 rows). A parameter minted in batch N+1 forces no re-scan of batches ≤N and nothing reads that fact. At 100 parameters × 53 sources the "absent" route is 5,300 rows. Acceptance: a derived ledger (source × parameter → observed / absent / not-scanned) with a check red when a catalogued parameter has unscanned sources.

**F14 · MEDIUM · gate (P6/P7 collision).** K02 (blocking) compares a live determination's junction against every extraction for its parameter "RIGHT NOW" (`test_db_integrity.py:1280-1290`); batch 16 retired spec 8 for this. P7's first live determination makes P6's next extraction on that parameter red until re-determined. Acceptance: the P6 loop states the engine re-run per touched parameter before capture.

**F15 · MEDIUM · gate (B6 paywall containment).** "Listed as leads in the catalogue's evidence-state column": `research_code_leads` has no parameter column [VERIFIED: PRAGMA], `EXHAUSTED` candidates need `found_under_slug` and an exec. Neither can say which parameter a paywalled code concerns; the column is underivable. Acceptance: a lead→parameter edge exists before the column claims it.

**F16 · MEDIUM · multi-term caps.** The remediation plan's 60-extraction cap and SUSTAINED-per-extraction comparator penalise breadth (one full ADA scan exceeds 60); the catalogue plan drops them silently and B6 moves review to the owner at thousands of rows. Acceptance: state the cap or its removal, and the review unit (per source).

**F17 · MEDIUM · P3 dead tables.** "Re-key or remove": committed data migrations `data_20260821185244` and `data_20260901183203` INSERT into item-keyed tables (rule 5: never dropped); ~21 non-migration callers across scripts/tools/schemas/governance/skills [VERIFIED: grep]; `schema_reference_audit` sweeps those but not prose. `site_pages_fresh` walks `items` (0 rows) — P5's "fresh-render checks" are vacuous by construction. Gates the plan forgets: `research_contract_sync` (blocking, index-0 hook), `migration_reproducibility` (counts only — an UPDATE to `base_parameters` is invisible), `identifier_floor_audit`, `jurisdiction_db_vocabulary` (worklist carries CH, UG), `derived_not_curated_audit`.

**F18 · LOW · S2.** Parameter 12's migration note says "no source adjudication behind it"; TERM-091 holds a NAMES-NEW adjudication (batch 20) [VERIFIED].

## C. SURVIVED

- Cross-slug extraction without a slug fiction: attacked via `insert_extraction` and the J01 note — held (ref↔slug only).
- Engine gathers by parameter, not slug: `assess_cell.gather_sources` 297-303 — held.
- Every Part A count listed in F9 — re-derived, held.
- R16 debt baseline (11 unadjudicated; 8 undisposed terms: TERM-016/053/075/079/090–094) — held.
- "No verb retires a parameter" — searched by verb name and by UPDATE statement — genuine absence.
- `a8b7c11` containment: migration header 9 inserts/0 updates/0 deletes; `base_parameters` 10 rows — held.
- "No adversarial pass required for vocabulary tables" — true of the RULE's limb (a) as parsed by `adversarial_pass_audit.py`; whether a judgment-stage vocabulary write may go unreviewed when standing subject 4 names it as the pass's subject is WITHHELD-FOR-OWNER.
- Owner's 2026-09-18 directive ("search by slug ... adjudicate by all slugs ... wherever is relevant ... can be mined") exists at `sessions/session_2026-09-18-research-batch-15-t2-synthesis-threshold.md:53` (grep -r; the Grep tool cannot see it). A2 omits it — the ruling nearest the owner's core requirement.

## D. THE GRAPH (stage · reads · writes · refuses · gates · conditionals · defects)

| stage | reads | writes | refuses | gates | conditional / defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| search `log-search` | slugs, evidence_sources | search_executions, search_admissions, artefacts | no prior; bad jurisdiction; admitted≠edges; origin≠planned with target | R8, R14, R1 (via target), v_coverage_* | slug NOT NULL; lead-index origin unused (F12) |
| screen `add-candidate` | exec, slugs, artefacts | search_candidates | surfaced_in not in bytes | RC1 blocking (surfaced_in only) | found_under_slug NOT NULL; optional (F12) |
| retrieve `retrieval_log.fetch` | web | retrieval-log manifest | — | author_fidelity (advisory, Crossref only) | no ref_id → UNSCOPED (F7) |
| admit `add-source` | stash, slugs | evidence_sources, authors, source_slug_links | dup DOI/key; merged slug | R9/R9a/R9b, R10, R13, C04, D04 | no exec needed (F12) |
| observe | evidence_sources | observed_terms | unknown ref; tombstone; term_id | R11-harvest | UNIQUE folds phrases (F3); no verbatim (F7) |
| adjudicate / add-term | observed_terms, terms | term_adjudications, terms | value-bearing name; existing name | R16-adjudicate | domain free text (F6); no amend (F5) |
| promote / decline | terms, declinations | base_parameters, parameter_declinations | declined term; dup; value name | R16, validate_parameters | no retire/merge/un-decline (F5); no pass (F11) |
| direction | base_parameters | UPDATE base_parameters | restating | none | write-once (F5); UPDATE invisible to migration_reproducibility |
| extract | links, params, artefacts | source_value_extractions, extraction_relations; UPDATE data_capture_status | ref∉slug link; inactive param; quote not in bytes; T4–6 without loc_* | extraction_relations_integrity, C06, K02 | slug NOT NULL but param↔slug free (F4); none written before P5 (F1) |
| relate | extractions | extraction_relations | self-edge; condition without row | extraction_relations_integrity | — |
| grade `add-population-match` | evidence_sources | evidence_population_match | — | R13 | required per admission (F12) |
| mine `log-mining` | source_slug_links | citation_mining | ref not linked to slug | R2, citation_mining_* | PK per slug (GAP-011, F4) |
| determine `assess_cell` | extractions (claim/derived), sources | specifications, links (scratch only) | canonical DB; --slug missing | K01, K02, validate_evidence_state | slug required (F4); K02 trap (F14) |
| render | items (0), specifications | parts/, site/, tools/ | — | site_pages_fresh (EXAMINED 0) | vacuous (F17) |

## E. NOT VERIFIED / NOT READ

"Two finished scans (52 items)" (task outputs end in interruption; count not found); "20 old per-item value files" (directory exists, not counted); EN 17210/CSA refusals taken from batch 22/23 records, not re-fetched; "ISO 21542, BS 8300... expected paywalled" untested; `citation_mining_session` level (saw advisory once, not confirmed); Stop-hook behaviour; overlap of `tier456-verified-sources.json` with `source_locators`; CI state of the branch; DR §12.1 step text beyond §12.2–12.5; `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` beyond `gather_sources`, `determine`, argparse.

## Structured findings, as the critic emitted them

```json
[
 {"lens":"L1-existence","subject_table":"observed_terms","claim_attacked":"D1/P2: every quoted phrase is checked against the text by script","verdict":"SUSTAINED","severity":"HIGH"},
 {"lens":"L2-fidelity","claim_attacked":"A4: owner said a skimmed figure may set a published value; Option A superseded","verdict":"SUSTAINED","severity":"HIGH"},
 {"lens":"L3-independence","claim_attacked":"A3/worklist: 76 distinct code-body leads in buckets 1-2 plus INT","verdict":"SUSTAINED","severity":"LOW"},
 {"lens":"L4-tier","verdict":"NOT-ATTACKED"},
 {"lens":"L5-population","subject_table":"source_value_extractions","claim_attacked":"D6: who it serves is empty until determinations exist","verdict":"SUSTAINED","severity":"MEDIUM"},
 {"lens":"L6-contrary","claim_attacked":"A2 lists the rulings that shape this work (omits the 2026-09-18 directive)","verdict":"SUSTAINED","severity":"MEDIUM"},
 {"lens":"L7-recognition","claim_attacked":"B2 Release 0 helps people ask the right questions (code-first, quantity-only shape vs the 2026-09-18 directive to mine logics, arguments and qualitative Co-1 findings)","verdict":"SUSTAINED","severity":"MEDIUM"},
 {"lens":"L8-query-shape","claim_attacked":"B6: no verb retires a parameter","verdict":"SURVIVED"},
 {"lens":"S1-harm-reached-row","subject_table":"evidence_sources","subject_key":"REF-00999","claim_attacked":"harm findings on ramps are held as re-verifiable evidence the catalogue can surface","verdict":"SUSTAINED","severity":"MEDIUM"},
 {"lens":"S2-mismatch-note-vs-payload","subject_table":"base_parameters","subject_key":"12","claim_attacked":"migration note: 'no source adjudication behind it'","verdict":"SUSTAINED","severity":"LOW"},
 {"lens":"S3-containment","subject_table":"base_parameters","claim_attacked":"a8b7c11 wrote nine parameter rows and nothing else to the database","verdict":"SURVIVED"}
]
```

## Orchestrator's spot-checks of the critic (2026-10-09)

- F9 persisted artefacts: re-derived. 49 of 53 admitted sources have an artefact file on disk (json 32, pdf 22, html 21, txt 14, png 13, xml 3, zip 1 counted per file); no artefact for REF-00990, REF-00991, REF-00999, REF-01000. **My plan v1 claim "full text saved for only 14 of 53" was wrong**: I had counted only derived `-text.txt` files. Text can be extracted from the PDFs and HTML already held.
- F3: `observe_term` does look up `(ref_id, surface_form, language)` first and returns the earlier row with `created: False` (read in `scripts/db.py`). Holds.
- F1/R16 text: `research_batch_dod.py` line 966 contains "on to carry an extraction is not read either." Holds.
- F7: `_require_verbatim` appears at `db.py:7049` (definition) and one call at `:7676`. Holds.
- F8: the transcript wording quoted by the critic matches what I asked and what the owner answered. The two readings (skimmed-grade versus pulled-from-another-slug) are both possible; the later owner statements about slug-independence corroborate the cross-slug reading. Neither should be recorded as settled.
- A claim in the critic's report that I found wrong: it says the database holds "0 PROPOSED" decisions in an earlier adjudication; not repeated here. The decisions table holds 2 PROPOSED (D-0139, D-0140).

"Interrogate quality, logic, sequencing and flexibility of pipeline all directions as well as all gates, reads, writes, conditionals. Ensure that all of our terms/parameter in catalogued will be leveraged in such a way where we can scrape information across any parameter if it appears in any source no matter the slug. Slugs guide our searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources! Our terms/parameter catalogue will, which means I expect harvesting across multiple terms if a source discusses multiple terms. Ensure that we can add and expand parameter catalogue as required based on new information we come across."
Earlier owner statements (quoted, not paraphrased): "while we search by slug, we scan each source for any and all applicable parameters. we may need to just prepopulate a parameters list."; "pull from the major codes, literature and advocacy from major countries"; "there should be an exhaustive bibliography that is outdated but correct that has info on each jurisdiction code bodies and major groups"; and the 2026-09-18 owner directive recorded in `sessions/session_2026-09-18-research-batch-15-t2-synthesis-threshold.md` around line 53 (find it with grep -r; it is the ruling nearest the core requirement and v1 omitted it). The owner complained about internal jargon: write for a non-programmer. Define every internal code (R16, K02, C10, DoD, stem, slug, and so on) in plain words the first time it appears, or avoid it.

WRONG: 49 of 53 admitted sources have an artefact file on disk (PDF, HTML, JSON, XML...); only REF-00990, REF-00991, REF-00999, REF-01000 have none; many lack a derived `-text.txt` that text extraction (pymupdf is installed) could produce. v1's "fetch again" also contradicted the owner's 2026-09-25 ruling that unreachable things are given up on. - Owner's answer "2 ..yes? like, one pulled from another slug? should be yes, but we still tag it for follow up later" answered the question "Does a preliminary or skim extraction ever govern a published cell?" It is AMBIGUOUS between (a) a skimmed-grade figure may govern, tagged for follow-up, and (b) an extraction pulled from a source filed under another slug is acceptable, tagged for follow-up. The owner's later statements corroborate (b) strongly. v2 must not record either as settled; it must quote the owner verbatim beside the question and carry the ambiguity as an open item, and design the typed follow-up marker the critique calls for.
- "A" (turn the 94 terms into quantities) answered a question about what the owner meant by "90+ cleaned parameters"; "pull from the major codes..." answered a separate question. Project rule (2026-09-09 owner ruling; `insert_term` in scripts/db.py): parameter names are minted only from a phrase an admitted source actually uses (`add-term --from-observation`), never invented. The owner said that ruling is theirs to revisit; do not assume it has been revisited.
- Nine parameters (ids 4 to 12) were promoted on a scratch copy and applied to the live database through migration `data_20261009055057_...sql`, committed `[skip ci]` on the work branch with no pull request, no session record, no attestation, direction left unset, and migration note text that is wrong for TERM-091. - The earlier plan's cap of 60 extractions came from the remediation plan's pilot, which was a different, narrower task. Decide what replaces it.

Put a plain-language executive summary (at most 350 words) FIRST, then a "How to read this" box, then:
1. WHAT CHANGED FROM v1 AND WHY: a table giving a disposition for EVERY critique finding (F1 to F18, plus the structured L5, L6, L7, S1 items): ACCEPTED / MODIFIED / REJECTED, with the evidence for the call. Judiciousness means you may reject a finding, but only with evidence and CLAUDE.md section 8 reasoning (adding apparatus carries the burden of proof; state what wrong thing reaches the guidebook without it, and what reads it). Verify every critique claim you rely on in the code or the database; the orchestrator spot-checked only a few.
2. STATE (re-derived, with the command beside each figure, CLAUDE.md rule 7a). Include corrected Part A material: persisted artefacts, partial texts, tombstoned source, `source_locators` (893 rows) as the largest lead list, worklist double-counts.
3. THE SCAN CONTRACT (the heart of the owner's requirement). Define precisely: slugs guide SEARCHES; the parameter catalogue (with its multilingual aliases, `term_aliases`) guides what is derived and mined from EVERY admitted source, whatever slug it was filed under. Specify: a closed-vocabulary pass (scan the source against all active parameters) and an open-vocabulary pass (find quantities not yet in the catalogue, to be proposed as new terms), what a scanner may and may not decide, what is verified by script versus judged and by whom, how a source that states many quantities in one clause or table yields many observations/extractions (including the fact that `observe_term` folds the same phrase twice in one source and one phrase can name two parameters), how cross-slug extraction is typed and followed up, what the extraction's `slug` value means, and how completeness of a scan is evidenced (a derived source-by-parameter scan ledger and what reads it). State which parts exist today in the code and which need new tooling.
4. CATALOGUE GROWTH PROTOCOL: every way the catalogue changes: add; add after sources were already scanned (backfill and the scan debt it creates); split; merge; rename; retire; disputed or wrong direction; new language alias; new jurisdiction or source family; superseded source. For each: the sanctioned path today, the refusals, what is irreversible, the cost at 1 term and at 100, and the tooling that must exist BEFORE mass promotion (the critique's F5: no retire, merge, rename or un-decline verb exists; `canonical_en` and `domain` cannot be amended; direction is write-once). Propose the minimum viable set and its sequencing, and say what stays out.
5. THE PIPELINE AS A GRAPH: a table of every stage (search, screen, retrieve, admit, observe, adjudicate, mint term, promote or decline, set direction, extract, relate, grade population match, mine citations, determine, render, and the new stages you propose) giving what it reads, writes, refuses, which gate fires (name, blocking or advisory, what it examines, whether it can pass vacuously), and its conditionals (what runs or is skipped under which state, including a session with no searches and no admissions). Include backward and re-entrant edges (new parameter to rescan old sources; new source to scan against the whole catalogue; superseded source; merged parameter to extraction pointers). Mark every gate the plan relies on, and every one it forgets that the critique lists.
6. ITEMS AND CATEGORIES (the owner's original ask): how catalogue items and categories are derived from the parameter catalogue, with the critique's repairs: parameter-to-element is many-to-many (verify on live parameters); categories come from a CHECK'd vocabulary the owner approves, not from the free-text `terms.domain` column; an item is a derived roll-up, never a key (owner ruling 2026-08-26); no item or category name may state a value or answer; check that goes red when an active parameter reaches no catalogue surface; the dead item-keyed tables and `site_pages_fresh` vacuity. What Release 0 can honestly show given that extractions, not parameter names, carry the content, and what the 2026-09-18 directive about mining arguments and qualitative Co-1 findings adds. The old A to K item index may be consulted only AFTER the derivation is frozen, as a coverage check, names only.
7. SEQUENCE: phases with explicit dependencies, which can run in parallel, and for each phase: reads, writes, which PR type (tooling merged first per rule 10; research; render), what stem and gating it uses (the critique's F2: research gates are scoped to a session's admissions; a harvest-only session has zero admissions; decide how cohorts are formed so that gates examine something), exit criteria, and what happens on failure. Cover acquisition from lead lists without a search (the critique's F12: `origin='lead-index'`, search-log rows, R13 population-match rows, no-DOI explanations, mining rows), reuse of already-persisted artefacts, the owner's bucket 1 and 2 scope ruling and how exhaustion is judged when coverage is by slug but the catalogue is by parameter, and the trap where a first live determination makes later extractions on the same parameter red (K02). Decide the review unit and volume policy for harvest-at-scale and who reviews vocabulary writes (the adversarial rule does not cover vocabulary tables; the critique says whether that is withheld for the owner).
8. GATES AND CHECKS: every gate touched, with EXAMINED subject, level, and the row that fails it today; every new check proposed with the wrong thing it prevents and what reads it; checks that would be vacuous on first run, flagged as such.
9. RISKS, with containment; and what the plan deliberately does NOT do.
10. DECISIONS FOR THE OWNER: numbered, plain, one question each, with your recommendation, the owner's verbatim words where they bear on it, and the effect of each answer on the sequence. Include the unresolved ambiguity above and the question of reviewing the nine promoted rows.
11. RECORD-KEEPING: what must be written to the ledger (`references/project-standards.md`) and where, with owner words verbatim; which supersessions rule 0 requires you to name (use the `SUPERSEDES: ... BY:` grammar documented in scripts/audit/supersession_backpointer_audit.py only as a description of what a later session must write, do not write it).
12. ACCEPTANCE TESTS AND RE-DERIVE COMMANDS: for each phase and each owner requirement, a test that could go red on the defect it addresses (CLAUDE.md section 5a), with the command that runs it.

## STANDARDS
- Verify against the repository; mark each load-bearing claim [VERIFIED: how] or [INFERRED] or [OPEN]. No hand-typed counts without the command that recomputes them.
- Honour the project rules: derive, do not curate (rule 8); point, do not copy (rule 5); research and tooling ship apart (rule 10); open the pull request last and do not watch it (rule 9); deletion is cheap and adding apparatus needs justification (section 8); the item layer is gone and `[A-Z]-NN` codes are never containers; no value in any name.
- Do not place the plan in `workplan/` or write a decision record; this is a session working paper. Do not invent facts about documents you have not read; if text is not persisted, say so.
- Canadian English. No flattery. Plain words. Tables where they help a human compare.
- Length: as long as exhaustive honesty requires, but keep the first page decision-ready; push mechanics into later sections.
- Your final message (not the file) must be at most 250 words: the path, the five most consequential changes from v1, the decisions the owner must make first, and anything you could not verify. Do not paste the plan.

1	# Catalogue plan, version 2: read every source for every parameter, grow the list safely, then derive items and categories
2	
3	Prepared 2026-10-09 in the batch 24 session, after the independent critique in `catalogue-plan-critique-fable.md` (same folder). This is a session working paper. It proposes. It decides nothing, records no ruling and changes no file but itself. Version 1 (`catalogue-plan.md`) stays as written; this replaces it for reading and deciding.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Executive summary
8	
9	**What this is.** A rewrite of the catalogue plan. An independent critique failed version 1 on three of your four requirements. This version is built to meet all four. Nothing happens until you answer section 10.
10	
11	**The core change.** Every source we hold is read against the whole parameter list, whatever topic folder ("slug") it came in under. Slugs stay what you said: search plans. Each reading leaves a record of which source was read, how much of its text, and against which version of the list. So for every source and every parameter the database can show: figure found, nothing found, or not yet read. When a parameter is added later, that record shows which earlier sources still need reading for it.
12	
13	**What we already hold.** Far more than version 1 said. Saved files contain the full text of most national codes we admitted, including those of the US, UK, Ireland, Japan, Korea, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Finland and New Zealand. Where batch 23's texts are partial, it is only because a few pages were pulled from PDFs we hold whole. The first research step needs no downloading.
14	
15	**Tooling first.** Before bulk additions, one tooling change adds what is missing: ways to retire, merge, rename and un-decline a parameter; a way to add aliases; a check that an observed phrase is really in the source; and a record of each reading.
16	
17	**Then research.** Small groups of sources, reviewed one source at a time, with no cap on how many figures a source yields. New documents come from the lists we hold, bucket 1 first.
18	
19	**The catalogue.** For the first release, one item per parameter, grouped into categories you approve once. It shows the questions, what each held code says (marked), qualitative and lived-experience findings, and where reading is incomplete. No determination is published yet.
20	
21	**Decide first (section 10):**
22	1. what your answer "2" meant (two readings are possible);
23	2. whether to keep the nine parameters already added;
24	3. whether names must still come only from a source's own phrase;
25	4. whether to approve the tooling list.
26	
27	---
28	
29	> ### How to read this
30	>
31	> **Order.** Sections 1 and 10 are for deciding. Sections 3, 4 and 6 are the design. Sections 5, 7, 8 and 12 are mechanics for the sessions that carry it out.
32	>
33	> **Labels on claims.** **[VERIFIED: how]** means checked in the repository or database for this paper, and the check is named. **[INFERRED]** means reasoned from verified facts but not tested. **[OPEN]** means not settled and not settleable without you or more work.
34	>
35	> **Numbers.** Every count sits beside the command that recomputes it (CLAUDE.md rule 7a). The numbers are as of 2026-10-09 and will move. Re-run the command rather than trusting the figure.
36	>
37	> **Plain words for the project's terms.**
38	>
39	> | Word | Meaning here |
40	> |---|---|
41	> | source | A document admitted into the evidence base, such as a building code, a study, a guide or a disability organization's statement. Each has an ID like REF-00987. |
42	> | slug | A topic folder that searches are planned and filed under, such as `accessible-circulation-geometry`. |
43	> | term | An entry in the project's vocabulary (a word or phrase with a definition). |
44	> | parameter | A term promoted to "a measurable design quantity the guidebook takes a position on", such as ramp gradient or door width. Parameters are numbered and a number is never reused. |
45	> | alias | Another way of writing a term, often in another language. |
46	> | observation | A record that a source uses a phrase, word for word, at a stated place in it. |
47	> | adjudication | The recorded judgment of what an observed phrase refers to: an existing term, a new term, not one of ours, or undecided. |
48	> | extraction | One thing a source says about one parameter, with its quote and location: a figure, a condition, a finding, an argument, or an explicit "sets nothing". |
49	> | determination | The guidebook's computed position on a parameter for a group of people. Stored in the `specifications` table. None is live today. |
50	> | scan | One reading of one source against the parameter list (defined fully in section 3). |
51	> | item, category, element | An **item** is a catalogue entry. A **category** is a browsing group of items. An **element** is the physical thing a quantity belongs to (door, ramp, toilet). |
52	> | cohort | The group of sources handled in one research session and one pull request. |
53	> | pull request (PR) | A proposed change you review and merge. A **tooling PR** changes the machinery. A **research PR** adds data. Project rule 10 says they never share a PR, and tooling merges first. |
54	> | migration | The append-only file that carries database changes into the shared database. |
55	> | check, gate | An automatic test. **Blocking** stops a merge, **advisory** only reports. A check is **vacuous** when it passes because it looked at nothing. |
56	> | the batch-completion gate | `scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py`, also called the definition of done (DoD). Its rules are numbered R1 to R16. The ones that matter here are below this table. |
57	> | session name | The label stamped on every row a session writes, such as `session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot`. Two pointer files hold such names. `scratchpad/CURRENT` names the session running now. `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH` names the last finished research batch. |
58	> | ledger | `references/project-standards.md`, where your rulings are recorded. |
59	> | tiers, markers | T1 is controlled research. Co-1 is lived experience or work by disabled people's organizations (co-primary with T1). T2 is a systematic review or synthesis. Co-2 is occupational-therapy professional guidance. T3 is lower-control research or grey literature. T4 to T6 are standards and codes. The markers are ● confirmed evidence, ◐ standards basis only (T4, T5), and ○ thin or code-floor (T3 grey, and T6 codes without research behind them). |
60	> | buckets | Your priority jurisdictions. Bucket 1 is UN, ISO, Canada, USA, UK, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Japan and Australia. Bucket 2 is EU, Singapore, New Zealand, Ireland, France, Spain, Portugal, Finland, Netherlands and South Korea. Re-derive with `sed -n '420,424p' workplan/2026-08-18-research-frame-proposal.md`. |
61	> | tombstone | A source replaced by a better copy. It is kept for history and never read again. |
62	>
63	> The batch-completion rules that matter here:
64	> - **R1:** some lived-experience work is present in the batch.
65	> - **R9a, R9b:** source IDs do not collide with ones already held.
66	> - **R11-harvest:** every admitted source has at least one observation.
67	> - **R13:** every T1 to T3 source has its study population graded against the population served.
68	> - **R16-adjudicate:** every observation is judged.
69	> - **R16:** every term a judgment names is promoted or declined.
70	>
71	> **K02** is the check that a live determination accounts for every figure on file for its parameter. **C10** is the check that a published value does not rest on an unverified source.
72	>
73	> **Where each of your four requirements is met.**
74	>
75	> | Your requirement (your words) | Met in |
76	> |---|---|
77	> | "Interrogate quality, logic, sequencing and flexibility of pipeline all directions as well as all gates, reads, writes, conditionals." | Section 5 (the graph, with backward edges), section 7 (sequence), section 8 (every gate) |

# Catalogue plan, version 2: read every source for every parameter, grow the list safely, then derive items and categories

Prepared 2026-10-09 in the batch 24 session, after the independent critique in `catalogue-plan-critique-fable.md` (same folder). This is a session working paper. It proposes. It decides nothing, records no ruling and changes no file but itself. Version 1 (`catalogue-plan.md`) stays as written; this replaces it for reading and deciding.

---

## Executive summary

**What this is.** A rewrite of the catalogue plan. An independent critique failed version 1 on three of your four requirements. This version is built to meet all four. Nothing happens until you answer section 10.

**The core change.** Every source we hold is read against the whole parameter list, whatever topic folder ("slug") it came in under. Slugs stay what you said: search plans. Each reading leaves a record of which source was read, how much of its text, and against which version of the list. So for every source and every parameter the database can show: figure found, nothing found, or not yet read. When a parameter is added later, that record shows which earlier sources still need reading for it.

**What we already hold.** Far more than version 1 said. Saved files contain the full text of most national codes we admitted, including those of the US, UK, Ireland, Japan, Korea, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Finland and New Zealand. Where batch 23's texts are partial, it is only because a few pages were pulled from PDFs we hold whole. The first research step needs no downloading.

**Tooling first.** Before bulk additions, one tooling change adds what is missing: ways to retire, merge, rename and un-decline a parameter; a way to add aliases; a check that an observed phrase is really in the source; and a record of each reading.

**Then research.** Small groups of sources, reviewed one source at a time, with no cap on how many figures a source yields. New documents come from the lists we hold, bucket 1 first.

**The catalogue.** For the first release, one item per parameter, grouped into categories you approve once. It shows the questions, what each held code says (marked), qualitative and lived-experience findings, and where reading is incomplete. No determination is published yet.

**Decide first (section 10):**
1. what your answer "2" meant (two readings are possible);
2. whether to keep the nine parameters already added;
3. whether names must still come only from a source's own phrase;
4. whether to approve the tooling list.

---

> ### How to read this
>
> **Order.** Sections 1 and 10 are for deciding. Sections 3, 4 and 6 are the design. Sections 5, 7, 8 and 12 are mechanics for the sessions that carry it out.
>
> **Labels on claims.** **[VERIFIED: how]** means checked in the repository or database for this paper, and the check is named. **[INFERRED]** means reasoned from verified facts but not tested. **[OPEN]** means not settled and not settleable without you or more work.
>
> **Numbers.** Every count sits beside the command that recomputes it (CLAUDE.md rule 7a). The numbers are as of 2026-10-09 and will move. Re-run the command rather than trusting the figure.
>
> **Plain words for the project's terms.**
>
> | Word | Meaning here |
> |---|---|
> | source | A document admitted into the evidence base, such as a building code, a study, a guide or a disability organization's statement. Each has an ID like REF-00987. |
> | slug | A topic folder that searches are planned and filed under, such as `accessible-circulation-geometry`. |
> | term | An entry in the project's vocabulary (a word or phrase with a definition). |
> | parameter | A term promoted to "a measurable design quantity the guidebook takes a position on", such as ramp gradient or door width. Parameters are numbered and a number is never reused. |
> | alias | Another way of writing a term, often in another language. |
> | observation | A record that a source uses a phrase, word for word, at a stated place in it. |
> | adjudication | The recorded judgment of what an observed phrase refers to: an existing term, a new term, not one of ours, or undecided. |
> | extraction | One thing a source says about one parameter, with its quote and location: a figure, a condition, a finding, an argument, or an explicit "sets nothing". |
> | determination | The guidebook's computed position on a parameter for a group of people. Stored in the `specifications` table. None is live today. |
> | scan | One reading of one source against the parameter list (defined fully in section 3). |
> | item, category, element | An **item** is a catalogue entry. A **category** is a browsing group of items. An **element** is the physical thing a quantity belongs to (door, ramp, toilet). |
> | cohort | The group of sources handled in one research session and one pull request. |
> | pull request (PR) | A proposed change you review and merge. A **tooling PR** changes the machinery. A **research PR** adds data. Project rule 10 says they never share a PR, and tooling merges first. |
> | migration | The append-only file that carries database changes into the shared database. |
> | check, gate | An automatic test. **Blocking** stops a merge, **advisory** only reports. A check is **vacuous** when it passes because it looked at nothing. |
> | the batch-completion gate | `scripts/audit/research_batch_dod.py`, also called the definition of done (DoD). Its rules are numbered R1 to R16. The ones that matter here are below this table. |
> | session name | The label stamped on every row a session writes, such as `session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot`. Two pointer files hold such names. `scratchpad/CURRENT` names the session running now. `sessions/LATEST-RESEARCH` names the last finished research batch. |
> | ledger | `references/project-standards.md`, where your rulings are recorded. |
> | tiers, markers | T1 is controlled research. Co-1 is lived experience or work by disabled people's organizations (co-primary with T1). T2 is a systematic review or synthesis. Co-2 is occupational-therapy professional guidance. T3 is lower-control research or grey literature. T4 to T6 are standards and codes. The markers are ● confirmed evidence, ◐ standards basis only (T4, T5), and ○ thin or code-floor (T3 grey, and T6 codes without research behind them). |
> | buckets | Your priority jurisdictions. Bucket 1 is UN, ISO, Canada, USA, UK, Germany, Norway, Sweden, Japan and Australia. Bucket 2 is EU, Singapore, New Zealand, Ireland, France, Spain, Portugal, Finland, Netherlands and South Korea. Re-derive with `sed -n '420,424p' workplan/2026-08-18-research-frame-proposal.md`. |
> | tombstone | A source replaced by a better copy. It is kept for history and never read again. |
>
> The batch-completion rules that matter here:
> - **R1:** some lived-experience work is present in the batch.
> - **R9a, R9b:** source IDs do not collide with ones already held.
> - **R11-harvest:** every admitted source has at least one observation.
> - **R13:** every T1 to T3 source has its study population graded against the population served.
> - **R16-adjudicate:** every observation is judged.
> - **R16:** every term a judgment names is promoted or declined.
>
> **K02** is the check that a live determination accounts for every figure on file for its parameter. **C10** is the check that a published value does not rest on an unverified source.
>
> **Where each of your four requirements is met.**
>
> | Your requirement (your words) | Met in |
> |---|---|
> | "Interrogate quality, logic, sequencing and flexibility of pipeline all directions as well as all gates, reads, writes, conditionals." | Section 5 (the graph, with backward edges), section 7 (sequence), section 8 (every gate) |
> | "scrape information across any parameter if it appears in any source no matter the slug. Slugs guide our searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources!" | Section 3 (scan contract), sections 3.7 and 7.4 (what a slug means, exhaustion by parameter) |
> | "I expect harvesting across multiple terms if a source discusses multiple terms." | Sections 3.3 to 3.5 (closed and open passes, one clause yielding many rows, one phrase naming two parameters) |
> | "Ensure that we can add and expand parameter catalogue as required based on new information we come across." | Section 4 (growth protocol and the tooling it needs), section 5.2 (re-reading old sources for new parameters) |

238	## 3. The scan contract
239	
240	### 3.1 The principle, in your words
241	
242	> "Slugs guide our searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources! Our terms/parameter catalogue will, which means I expect harvesting across multiple terms if a source discusses multiple terms."
243	
244	So:
245	- **Slugs decide what to look for and where.** That is search planning, search logging, and search coverage by jurisdiction.
246	- **The parameter catalogue decides what is taken from every admitted source.** That holds whatever slug the source came in under, and the catalogue's aliases help the reader recognize parameters in other languages.
247	
248	### 3.2 Definitions
249	
250	- **Source in scope.** An admitted source that is not a tombstone.
251	- **Catalogue.** The active parameters, with their terms, definitions, aliases and the phrases sources have already been observed using for them.
252	- **Catalogue version.** The highest parameter number that exists when a reading starts. Numbers are never reused (`base_parameters` is AUTOINCREMENT), so "version N" means exactly "parameters 1 to N, those active at the time". **[VERIFIED: DDL comment]**
253	- **Scan.** One reading of one source.
254	  - In **catalogue mode** it covers every active parameter up to the catalogue version.
255	  - In **targeted mode** it covers one named parameter (used for back-filling, section 5.2).
256	  - Every scan states its **text scope**: full, partial (pages a to b of N), fragment, or abstract. It also states which saved file it read, by checksum.
257	- **Closed pass.** Looking for every parameter already in the catalogue.
258	- **Open pass.** Looking for design quantities and qualities the catalogue lacks.
259	
260	### 3.3 The closed pass (every source, every parameter)
261	
262	For each source in scope, in catalogue mode:
263	
264	1. **Get the whole text.** Use the saved text. Where only a PDF is held, extract all pages with page markers and register the result under the source's ID (section 2.2, classes A′, B and C). No network.
265	2. **Pre-screen by script (optional; no judgment).** List the passages where any catalogue term, any alias, or any phrase already observed for a parameter occurs, with page and position. This is a reading aid. It never stands in for reading the text.
266	3. **Read the whole text against the whole list.** For every passage that states anything about a catalogued parameter (a figure, a range, a condition, a qualitative finding, an argument, or an explicit statement that it sets nothing), write:
267	   - an **observation** of the source's own phrase at that place, judged NAMES-EXISTING to the parameter's term;
268	   - **one extraction per thing said per parameter**, with the verbatim quote, the structured locator for codes, the figure role, the comparator, at least one lens, and relations such as "applies only when" (`relate-extraction … condition_on`).
269	4. **Record the reading** with its text scope, the file read, the catalogue version, and "open pass done: yes/no".
270	
271	Your 2026-09-18 directive applies at step 3. Arguments and qualitative findings are recorded, not just numbers. `claim_type` already allows `qualitative` and `framework`, and `figure_role` allows `finding`. **[VERIFIED: DDL]**
272	
273	### 3.4 The open pass (new quantities)
274	
275	In the same reading:
276	
277	1. Observe, verbatim, every phrase the source treats as a design quantity or quality and that the catalogue does not hold.
278	2. Judge each one:
279	   - NAMES-EXISTING, if it is another name for something we hold; this also proposes a source-attested alias;
280	   - NAMES-NEW through `add-term --from-observation`, if a reviewer would accept it as a new concept;
281	   - DEFERRED, if it cannot be settled from this source;
282	   - NOT-OURS.
283	3. Collect the NAMES-NEW terms into the cohort's **vocabulary review table**. It gives one row per proposed parameter: the source phrase and place, the session's recommendation (promote, decline, or merge into an existing parameter), and the reason.
284	4. Only after review are terms promoted (`add-parameter`) or declined (`decline-parameter`, with reason). Then the cohort's sources get **targeted** readings for the newly promoted parameters, in the same PR.
285	
286	A scanner may not mint a parameter by itself. An extraction can only point at a parameter that exists (`parameter_id NOT NULL`, refused unless active). **[VERIFIED: DDL and `insert_extraction`]**
287	
288	### 3.5 Many quantities in one clause; one phrase naming two quantities
289	
290	- **One clause states several quantities.** Write one extraction per quantity. They can share the same quote; each row's quote must contain its own figure (the digits check). **[VERIFIED: `_require_verbatim`]** Nothing stops several rows per source and parameter; this is the ruled one-to-many fan-out (D-0168), and a blocking check pins it (`judgment_handoff_shape`). **[VERIFIED: read]**
291	- **One phrase is used for two quantities.** For example, "clear width" at a door clause and at a route clause. Today the second sighting folds into the first and returns `created: False`, losing its place and quote. The second sense is then never judged.
292	  - **Repair (tooling T1):** an observation becomes one sighting. The uniqueness key gains the locator, so each sighting is judged separately. One sighting can name a door width and the other a corridor width.
293	  - A deliberate second judgment of one sighting stays what it is today: a contest, not a second meaning.
294	- **One quantity under many phrases and languages.** Each phrase is its own observation, judged to the same term. The phrase then becomes a candidate, source-attested alias (section 3.9).
295	
296	### 3.6 Who decides what
297	
298	| Act | Decided by | Verified by script | Recorded in |
299	|---|---|---|---|
300	| Text scope and pages read | Script (page markers against PDF page count) | Yes | Reading record |
301	| The phrase is in the source, at that place | Scanner quotes it | **Yes**: the quote is in the source's own saved file (scoped) and the phrase is inside the quote (new in T1 for observations; exists for extractions) | `observed_terms`, `source_value_extractions.claim_text` |
302	| The figure is in the quote | Scanner | **Yes**, digits including CJK numerals (exists) | Extraction |
303	| Which parameter a passage concerns | **Scanner (judgment)**, with a rationale | No; sampled by the independent review once per source | Adjudication rationale, extraction |
304	| Figure role, comparator, claim type, relations | Scanner | Vocabulary only, from the column CHECKs (exists) | Extraction |
305	| Which group a finding concerns (lens) | Scanner, from the source's own scope | Code must exist in its registry (exists) | Extraction lens columns |
306	| A phrase names a new concept | Scanner proposes | Name refused if it carries a digit, a comparator or a min/max word (exists) | `terms` plus NAMES-NEW |
307	| Promote, decline, merge, split, rename, retire | **You, or a reviewer you name (D5)** | The refusals of each verb | `base_parameters`, `parameter_declinations`, notes |
308	| Direction (which way is better) | Session, only when an admitted source states it; reviewed | Write-once (exists) | `base_parameters` |
309	| Category vocabulary and order | **You, once (D7)** | Name guard | Category registry (T2) |
310	| Placing a parameter in a category | Session, with warrant | Category must be in the registry | Assignment table (T2) |
311	| Tier | Derived from evidence type and scope | Yes (exists) | Source |
312	| Determination | **Engine only** (2026-09-09 ruling) | K01, K02, C10 | `specifications` |
313	
314	**A scanner may not:**
315	- promote, decline, retire, merge or rename a parameter;
316	- set a direction without a source's statement;
317	- add a jurisdiction, category or lens code;
318	- write a determination;
319	- add a slug link just to relabel an extraction.
320	
321	### 3.7 What `slug` means on an extraction, and the "other slug" follow-up
322	
323	- **Meaning.** `source_value_extractions.slug` records **which filing the source came in under**. v2 fixes the convention: use the slug of the search that admitted the source, reached through `search_admissions`. It says nothing about which topic the parameter belongs to. The table's own DDL comment already says this ("says the reading happened there"). **[VERIFIED: DDL]** `add-extraction` requires the source to be linked to that slug, and it deliberately does not check the parameter against the slug (`test_db_integrity.py`, J01 retirement note). **[VERIFIED: read]** So the closed pass needs no "slug fiction".
324	- **Rule for every reader:** no catalogue surface groups or filters by `extraction.slug`. The only slug-keyed views are search-plan views (`v_coverage_jurisdiction` and the others).
325	- **The follow-up marker.** Your answer "2" asks for a tag "for follow up later". What a tag means depends on D1:
326	  - Under reading **(a)**, the tag already exists. `extraction_method='skim'` and `extraction_status='preliminary'` are typed columns. What is missing is any reader: `assess_cell.py` contains no reference to either column. **[VERIFIED: `grep -c "extraction_status\|extraction_method" scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` gives 0]** A second home for the same fact would break rule 5. So v2 adds no new column for (a). It adds a reader: the engine report and the catalogue mark any value-setting figure that is skimmed or preliminary, and an advisory check lists live determinations resting on one.
327	  - Under reading **(b)**, nothing records that a figure was read outside the purpose its source was admitted for. Nothing can derive it either, because no slug-to-parameter map exists, and building one would be curation. v2 proposes a small typed table, `extraction_follow_ups`:
328	    - one row per open follow-up on an extraction;
329	    - a reason from a CHECK list (starting with `read-outside-admitting-purpose`);
330	    - a required warrant sentence;
331	    - who raised it, and who resolved it, when and how.
332	
333	    It is written by the scanner's judgment and read by the catalogue and by the same advisory check.
334	  - **Caution under (b).** Once every source is read for every parameter, most figures in a whole-code reading are "from another slug". Tagging all of them makes the tag noise. v2 therefore proposes that under (b) the scanner tags only figures a reviewer should re-check against the parameter's own literature, and states why on each row.
335	  - Neither table nor reader is built until you answer D1.
336	
337	### 3.8 Evidence that a scan is complete
338	
339	- **Reading record (new table, tooling T1): `source_scans`.**
340	  - **Fields:** source, mode (catalogue or targeted), catalogue version or target parameter, text scope with pages read and pages total, the checksum of the file read, open pass done, method (full read or pre-screen only), session.
341	  - **Writer:** `db.py record-scan`.
342	  - **It refuses:**
343	    - a tombstone;
344	    - a file not saved for that source;
345	    - "full" when the derived text's pages are fewer than the PDF's;
346	    - a typed-in catalogue version. The command computes it, never the person (rule 8).
347	- **Ledger (derived view): `v_scan_ledger`.** One row per source in scope and active parameter, with a status:
348	  - EXTRACTED: at least one non-absent extraction;
349	  - STATED-ABSENT: an extraction of type `absent`, meaning the source addresses the quantity and sets nothing;

## 3. The scan contract

### 3.1 The principle, in your words

> "Slugs guide our searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources! Our terms/parameter catalogue will, which means I expect harvesting across multiple terms if a source discusses multiple terms."

So:
- **Slugs decide what to look for and where.** That is search planning, search logging, and search coverage by jurisdiction.
- **The parameter catalogue decides what is taken from every admitted source.** That holds whatever slug the source came in under, and the catalogue's aliases help the reader recognize parameters in other languages.

### 3.2 Definitions

- **Source in scope.** An admitted source that is not a tombstone.
- **Catalogue.** The active parameters, with their terms, definitions, aliases and the phrases sources have already been observed using for them.
- **Catalogue version.** The highest parameter number that exists when a reading starts. Numbers are never reused (`base_parameters` is AUTOINCREMENT), so "version N" means exactly "parameters 1 to N, those active at the time". **[VERIFIED: DDL comment]**
- **Scan.** One reading of one source.
  - In **catalogue mode** it covers every active parameter up to the catalogue version.
  - In **targeted mode** it covers one named parameter (used for back-filling, section 5.2).
  - Every scan states its **text scope**: full, partial (pages a to b of N), fragment, or abstract. It also states which saved file it read, by checksum.
- **Closed pass.** Looking for every parameter already in the catalogue.
- **Open pass.** Looking for design quantities and qualities the catalogue lacks.

### 3.3 The closed pass (every source, every parameter)

For each source in scope, in catalogue mode:

1. **Get the whole text.** Use the saved text. Where only a PDF is held, extract all pages with page markers and register the result under the source's ID (section 2.2, classes A′, B and C). No network.
2. **Pre-screen by script (optional; no judgment).** List the passages where any catalogue term, any alias, or any phrase already observed for a parameter occurs, with page and position. This is a reading aid. It never stands in for reading the text.
3. **Read the whole text against the whole list.** For every passage that states anything about a catalogued parameter (a figure, a range, a condition, a qualitative finding, an argument, or an explicit statement that it sets nothing), write:
   - an **observation** of the source's own phrase at that place, judged NAMES-EXISTING to the parameter's term;
   - **one extraction per thing said per parameter**, with the verbatim quote, the structured locator for codes, the figure role, the comparator, at least one lens, and relations such as "applies only when" (`relate-extraction … condition_on`).
4. **Record the reading** with its text scope, the file read, the catalogue version, and "open pass done: yes/no".

Your 2026-09-18 directive applies at step 3. Arguments and qualitative findings are recorded, not just numbers. `claim_type` already allows `qualitative` and `framework`, and `figure_role` allows `finding`. **[VERIFIED: DDL]**

### 3.4 The open pass (new quantities)

In the same reading:

1. Observe, verbatim, every phrase the source treats as a design quantity or quality and that the catalogue does not hold.
2. Judge each one:
   - NAMES-EXISTING, if it is another name for something we hold; this also proposes a source-attested alias;
   - NAMES-NEW through `add-term --from-observation`, if a reviewer would accept it as a new concept;
   - DEFERRED, if it cannot be settled from this source;
   - NOT-OURS.
3. Collect the NAMES-NEW terms into the cohort's **vocabulary review table**. It gives one row per proposed parameter: the source phrase and place, the session's recommendation (promote, decline, or merge into an existing parameter), and the reason.
4. Only after review are terms promoted (`add-parameter`) or declined (`decline-parameter`, with reason). Then the cohort's sources get **targeted** readings for the newly promoted parameters, in the same PR.

A scanner may not mint a parameter by itself. An extraction can only point at a parameter that exists (`parameter_id NOT NULL`, refused unless active). **[VERIFIED: DDL and `insert_extraction`]**

### 3.5 Many quantities in one clause; one phrase naming two quantities

- **One clause states several quantities.** Write one extraction per quantity. They can share the same quote; each row's quote must contain its own figure (the digits check). **[VERIFIED: `_require_verbatim`]** Nothing stops several rows per source and parameter; this is the ruled one-to-many fan-out (D-0168), and a blocking check pins it (`judgment_handoff_shape`). **[VERIFIED: read]**
- **One phrase is used for two quantities.** For example, "clear width" at a door clause and at a route clause. Today the second sighting folds into the first and returns `created: False`, losing its place and quote. The second sense is then never judged.
  - **Repair (tooling T1):** an observation becomes one sighting. The uniqueness key gains the locator, so each sighting is judged separately. One sighting can name a door width and the other a corridor width.
  - A deliberate second judgment of one sighting stays what it is today: a contest, not a second meaning.
- **One quantity under many phrases and languages.** Each phrase is its own observation, judged to the same term. The phrase then becomes a candidate, source-attested alias (section 3.9).

### 3.6 Who decides what

| Act | Decided by | Verified by script | Recorded in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text scope and pages read | Script (page markers against PDF page count) | Yes | Reading record |
| The phrase is in the source, at that place | Scanner quotes it | **Yes**: the quote is in the source's own saved file (scoped) and the phrase is inside the quote (new in T1 for observations; exists for extractions) | `observed_terms`, `source_value_extractions.claim_text` |
| The figure is in the quote | Scanner | **Yes**, digits including CJK numerals (exists) | Extraction |
| Which parameter a passage concerns | **Scanner (judgment)**, with a rationale | No; sampled by the independent review once per source | Adjudication rationale, extraction |
| Figure role, comparator, claim type, relations | Scanner | Vocabulary only, from the column CHECKs (exists) | Extraction |
| Which group a finding concerns (lens) | Scanner, from the source's own scope | Code must exist in its registry (exists) | Extraction lens columns |
| A phrase names a new concept | Scanner proposes | Name refused if it carries a digit, a comparator or a min/max word (exists) | `terms` plus NAMES-NEW |
| Promote, decline, merge, split, rename, retire | **You, or a reviewer you name (D5)** | The refusals of each verb | `base_parameters`, `parameter_declinations`, notes |
| Direction (which way is better) | Session, only when an admitted source states it; reviewed | Write-once (exists) | `base_parameters` |
| Category vocabulary and order | **You, once (D7)** | Name guard | Category registry (T2) |
| Placing a parameter in a category | Session, with warrant | Category must be in the registry | Assignment table (T2) |
| Tier | Derived from evidence type and scope | Yes (exists) | Source |
| Determination | **Engine only** (2026-09-09 ruling) | K01, K02, C10 | `specifications` |

**A scanner may not:**
- promote, decline, retire, merge or rename a parameter;
- set a direction without a source's statement;
- add a jurisdiction, category or lens code;
- write a determination;
- add a slug link just to relabel an extraction.

### 3.7 What `slug` means on an extraction, and the "other slug" follow-up

- **Meaning.** `source_value_extractions.slug` records **which filing the source came in under**. v2 fixes the convention: use the slug of the search that admitted the source, reached through `search_admissions`. It says nothing about which topic the parameter belongs to. The table's own DDL comment already says this ("says the reading happened there"). **[VERIFIED: DDL]** `add-extraction` requires the source to be linked to that slug, and it deliberately does not check the parameter against the slug (`test_db_integrity.py`, J01 retirement note). **[VERIFIED: read]** So the closed pass needs no "slug fiction".
- **Rule for every reader:** no catalogue surface groups or filters by `extraction.slug`. The only slug-keyed views are search-plan views (`v_coverage_jurisdiction` and the others).
- **The follow-up marker.** Your answer "2" asks for a tag "for follow up later". What a tag means depends on D1:
  - Under reading **(a)**, the tag already exists. `extraction_method='skim'` and `extraction_status='preliminary'` are typed columns. What is missing is any reader: `assess_cell.py` contains no reference to either column. **[VERIFIED: `grep -c "extraction_status\|extraction_method" scripts/assess/assess_cell.py` gives 0]** A second home for the same fact would break rule 5. So v2 adds no new column for (a). It adds a reader: the engine report and the catalogue mark any value-setting figure that is skimmed or preliminary, and an advisory check lists live determinations resting on one.
  - Under reading **(b)**, nothing records that a figure was read outside the purpose its source was admitted for. Nothing can derive it either, because no slug-to-parameter map exists, and building one would be curation. v2 proposes a small typed table, `extraction_follow_ups`:
    - one row per open follow-up on an extraction;
    - a reason from a CHECK list (starting with `read-outside-admitting-purpose`);
    - a required warrant sentence;
    - who raised it, and who resolved it, when and how.

    It is written by the scanner's judgment and read by the catalogue and by the same advisory check.
  - **Caution under (b).** Once every source is read for every parameter, most figures in a whole-code reading are "from another slug". Tagging all of them makes the tag noise. v2 therefore proposes that under (b) the scanner tags only figures a reviewer should re-check against the parameter's own literature, and states why on each row.
  - Neither table nor reader is built until you answer D1.

### 3.8 Evidence that a scan is complete

- **Reading record (new table, tooling T1): `source_scans`.**
  - **Fields:** source, mode (catalogue or targeted), catalogue version or target parameter, text scope with pages read and pages total, the checksum of the file read, open pass done, method (full read or pre-screen only), session.
  - **Writer:** `db.py record-scan`.
  - **It refuses:**
    - a tombstone;
    - a file not saved for that source;
    - "full" when the derived text's pages are fewer than the PDF's;
    - a typed-in catalogue version. The command computes it, never the person (rule 8).
- **Ledger (derived view): `v_scan_ledger`.** One row per source in scope and active parameter, with a status:
  - EXTRACTED: at least one non-absent extraction;
  - STATED-ABSENT: an extraction of type `absent`, meaning the source addresses the quantity and sets nothing;
  - READ-NOTHING-FOUND: a full catalogue-mode or targeted reading covers it and found no row;
  - READ-PARTIAL: only partial, fragment or abstract readings cover it;
  - NOT-READ.

  Explicit "absent" rows stay for positive statements of absence. Silence is derived, so nobody writes an "absent" row for every source-parameter pair.
- **What reads it:**
  - the catalogue's evidence-state line;
  - the parameter-by-jurisdiction coverage view (section 7.4);
  - the advisory **scan-debt** check (section 8.2);
  - the new batch rule **R16-scan**: every admission in the batch has a catalogue-mode reading;
  - the worklist for back-filling (section 5.2).
- **Why it earns its place (section 8 test).** Without it, the catalogue can say or imply "no code sets a requirement" where nobody read the code for that quantity. ### 5.2 Backward and re-entrant edges

1. **New parameter, old sources.** A parameter numbered P, promoted in cohort N, leaves every earlier catalogue-mode reading with version below P as NOT-READ for P in the ledger. The pre-screen script lists candidate passages across all held texts. The next cohort does targeted readings for those hits. Sources with no hit get a targeted reading in "pre-screen only" mode, which the ledger shows as weaker than a full read. The scan-debt check counts what remains.
2. **New source, whole catalogue.** Every admission gets a catalogue-mode reading in its own session. R16-scan enforces this.
3. **New alias.** Re-run the pre-screen. A new hit in a source already read becomes a targeted reading.
4. **Superseded source.**
   - `supersede-source` first.
   - The tombstone leaves the ledger, and its readings stay as history.
   - The replacement gets a catalogue-mode reading.
   - Any live determination its figures fed is re-run (K01, K02).
5. **Merge.**
   - Extractions are re-pointed by the merge command, with a note.
   - Any live determination on either parameter is retired first, then re-run.
   - K02 enforces this.
6. **Split.** Mint the new parameters from observations, retire the old one, then re-read the clauses behind the old parameter's extractions in targeted mode for each new parameter. Old rows stay, as history on a retired parameter.
7. **Rename.** No pointer moves. The old name becomes a DEPRECATED alias. Render regenerates.
8. **Retire.** Readers filter it. Its extractions stay. Any live determination is retired first.
9. **Search under slug S admits a document.** It is read for all parameters, and its figures for parameters other slugs plan for are filed under S's admission. This is the owner's rule working, not a fault.
10. **Independent review finding.** It is corrected in the same pass, by migration, and may trigger a targeted re-read.
11. **Reasoning documents produce leads.** This is normal re-entry (CLAUDE.md §3). Leads go to the lead lists, never straight into the catalogue.
12. **Your ruling.** It is recorded on contact (rule 0). It may change gates, and any supersession is named (section 11).

### 5.3 Gates this plan relies on, and gates v1 forgot

- **Relied on:**
  - the batch gate (`research_dod_session`) and its corpus ratchet;
  - `test_db_integrity` (C06, K01, K02, C10);
  - `extraction_relations_integrity`, `judgment_handoff_shape`;
  - `alias_provenance_audit`, `jurisdiction_db_vocabulary`, `identifier_floor_audit`;
  - `schema_reference_audit`, `derived_not_curated_audit`, `column_vocabulary_audit`;
  - `research_contract_sync`, `research_dod_selftest`;
  - the two blocking render-freshness checks;
  - the attestation gates;
  - `adversarial_pass_audit` (through `/batch-done`).
- **Forgotten by v1 and now named:**
  - `research_contract_sync`, which a new R-rule triggers;
  - `migration_reproducibility`, which cannot see updates;
  - `identifier_floor_audit`, which argues against reverting the nine;

Opus's rewrite is at `scratchpad/session_2026-10-09-research-batch-24-parameter-pilot/catalogue-plan-v2.md` (about 17,000 words, pushed as `d52a5e6`). It starts with a one-page summary and a plain-words key. Its section 1 gives a decision on every one of the critic's findings, accepting, modifying or rejecting each with evidence. The summary names four decisions for you first (D1, D2, D3, D8, below).

**How v2 meets your four requirements**
- **Slug-independent mining:** every admitted source is read against the whole parameter list, whatever slug it came in under. Slugs stay as search plans.
- **Reading record:** each reading is recorded, with what text was read and against which version of the list. A view derived from those records then shows, for every source and parameter, one of three states: figure found, nothing found, or not yet read.
- **Multi-term harvest:** one clause can yield many rows. One phrase can name two parameters, because each sighting of a phrase becomes its own observation. There is no cap on figures per source. A source is reviewed one at a time.
- **Growth:** a new parameter added later shows which earlier sources still need reading for it. Tooling to retire, merge, rename, un-decline and add aliases is built before any bulk additions. The critic's check turned up that no command writes aliases at all.
- **Held sources:** most national codes we admitted are held in full, including the US ADA, UK Approved Document M, Ireland (two editions), the IPC guide and a 120-page ISO 21542 draft. The first research step therefore needs no downloading.

**What I checked myself**
- I confirmed the held files are the sizes claimed.
- I confirmed your "pull from the major codes" message was queued at 06:07:12, before my "slug by slug / you seed it" options arrived at 06:07:27. So that choice was never answered.
- I confirmed the correction that v1 wrongly said only 14 of 53 sources had saved text.
- I read the summary and sections 1 to 5, 7, 10 and 11. I did not read sections 6, 8, 9 and 12 (items and categories, the gate inventory, risks, and the acceptance tests).
- One design choice to weigh: each re-reading session also admits one new document so its own gate has something to check. That is a workaround for how the gates are scoped, and you may prefer a different arrangement.

**Decisions you need to make first**
- **D1:** what did your answer "2" mean? Your two options:
  - May a figure that was only skimmed set a published value, if it is tagged for follow-up? The plan recommends no.
  - May a figure from a source filed under another slug do so? The plan recommends yes.
- **D2:** keep the nine parameters already added, and carry them to the shared branch through a pull request with review? The plan recommends yes.
- **D3:** must parameter names still come only from a phrase a source uses? Your 2026-09-09 rule says so. The plan keeps the rule and uses your option A list as a checklist for readers.
- **D8:** approve the tooling list so it can ship first?

Nothing else has been written to the database or the ledger, and there is still no pull request. The critique of v1 overrode your 2026-08-19 rule on critiques of plans for this one plan only. A further critique of v2 would need your fresh request.
