3586	## Owner statement 2026-09-16 — dose-response evidence may be reasoned to a range, AS A PROXY
3587	
3588	> **"even if they aren't asserting a gradient, they are examining the impacts of gradients … this
3589	> means that adjudication will be able to reason that whatever range of gradients corresponds to
3590	> the best outcomes is the best range of gradient"**
3591	>
3592	> and, on being shown the limit of that inference:
3593	>
3594	> **"yes it's not perfect it's a proxy"**
3595	
3596	**WHAT THIS SETTLES.** A source that measures the EFFECT of a parameter without prescribing a value
3597	is not silent about that parameter, and judgment may reason from it toward a range. Batch 08 graded
3598	four such sources and the engine returned `pending` with `refs=0`, which reads as "no evidence" over
3599	two studies that measured articular discomfort rising 14→36% and pushrim force more than doubling.
3600	That reading is wrong, and the mechanism is what makes it wrong: `assess_cell.gather_sources()`
3601	gathers `figure_role IN ('claim','derived')` only, so a `finding` contributes nothing to a
3602	determination however much it measured.
3603	
3604	**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the limit is the owner's own word — PROXY.** The inference "best
3605	outcomes therefore best range" has a degenerate solution on the evidence as it stands: both curves
3606	are monotonic with no reported plateau, so "best" resolves to 0°, which is not a ramp. A ramp exists
3607	to change level, so the design question is the MAXIMUM ACCEPTABLE gradient, and that needs a
3608	threshold of acceptability which no admitted source supplies. Reasoning from dose-response to a
3609	range is therefore a proxy step and must be marked as one, never recorded as though a source had
3610	stated the value.
3611	
3612	**THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS THE VOCABULARY FOR "PROXY" AND SHOULD USE IT HERE.**
3613	`evidence_population_match.match_grade` carries PROXY for population-of-study vs population-served;
3614	`source_value_extractions.value_directness` exists for how directly evidence bears on the claim and
3615	sits at `NOT_ASSESSED` on every row because no grading rule has been ratified — which
3616	`workplan/2026-09-10-road-to-batch-06.md` makes STOP CONDITION 4, "inventing one is a stop
3617	condition". This statement is NOT read as ratifying a directness scale; it is read as ruling that
3618	the proxy inference is ADMISSIBLE and must be MARKED. The scale itself is still owed.
3619	
3620	**A LEAD THIS OPENS, recorded as a lead and not as a finding.** REF-00985 tested `0° to 4.8°`, and
3621	`arctan(1/12) = 4.76°` — 1:12 being the ramp ceiling in ADA, AS 1428.1, BS 8300-1 and others. If
3622	that ceiling is why 4.8° was chosen, the study measures discomfort across exactly the code-permitted
3623	range and finds it climbing throughout, which under the 2026-09-13 ruling ("a finding that a CODE is
3624	insufficient supplies no value, and is still first-class evidence") makes it a code-insufficiency
3625	finding rather than a bare dose-response curve. THE ABSTRACT DOES NOT SAY THIS. It is an inference
3626	from arithmetic and must be confirmed against the full text before it is filed as anything.
3627	
3628	CONDITION: Any session determining a cell whose evidence measures effects rather than stating values;
3629	any session implementing how `finding` rows reach a determination.
3630	ACTION: (1) A determination may rest on dose-response findings, marked as a proxy, never as a stated
3631	value. (2) `assess_cell` must be able to reach a determination from findings plus a threshold, not
3632	only from `claim` rows — today it cannot, and that is why batch 08 reads `refs=0`. (3) The threshold
3633	half is a code value or an equivalent criterion, and `research_code_leads` names which documents to
3634	fetch but deliberately holds no values (2026-08-12 REFERENCE-ONLY ruling), so it must be retrieved.
3635	(4) Do not invent a `value_directness` scale on the strength of this statement.
3636	DATE: 2026-09-16 — owner statement, quoted above.
3637	
3638	## Owner ruling 2026-09-17 — PRESENT BOTH notations; never choose between ratio and percentage
3639	
3640	> **"Present both--don't choose between ratio or percentage."**
3641	
3642	**WHAT THIS ANSWERS.** The `DEC` gap raised the same day by the ACTION (2) engine work. A gradient is
3643	written as a ratio (`1:12`, `1:20`) by some sources and as a percentage (`5 %`, `6 %`) by others, and
3644	they are the same physical quantity in two notations. `parse_bound` returns `None` for a ratio by
3645	explicit design, so `compose_value` was building the determination's interval out of the
3646	percentage-stated rows alone — measured on parameter 3: **2 of 7 governing claims**, with five rows
3647	dropped. Migration 086 made that visible in `value_note` instead of silent. The question it left open
3648	was whether the engine may convert, and the answer is that the question was malformed: **the engine
3649	does not pick a notation at all. It presents both.**
3650	
3651	**WHAT IT SETTLES.**
3652	
3653	1. **No notation is dropped.** A governing claim stated as a ratio contributes to the determination on
3654	   the same footing as one stated as a percentage. The 2-of-7 composition was a defect, not a policy.
3655	2. **No notation is privileged.** The determination does not select a "canonical" form and relegate the
3656	   other to a note. Both are carried, and a render surface shows both.
3657	3. **Conversion is for COMPARISON, not for replacement.** The engine must compare across notations to
3658	   apply the most-accommodating rule at all, and `1:20 = 5 %` exactly. That comparison is arithmetic.
3659	   What it must not do is overwrite what a source wrote with the other form.
3660	
3661	**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the limit is arithmetic rather than doctrine.** Some conversions are
3662	exact and some are not: `1:20` is exactly `5 %`, but `1:12` is `8.333…%` and no finite decimal is the
3663	figure the source stated. So a derived notation is **marked as derived**, and where it does not
3664	terminate it is marked as inexact as well. Presenting both does not license presenting a rounded
3665	figure as though a source had written it — that is the 2026-08-19 shape, one column along.
3666	
3667	**A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING.** Until this ruling the engine's protection against inventing figures
3668	was to refuse cross-unit composition outright, which cost it five of seven rows on the first cell it
3669	determined. The protection was real and the cost was invisible. Both halves of that stay true and the
3670	remedy is not to relax the refusal but to stop treating two notations of one quantity as two units.
3671	
3672	CONDITION: Any session composing a determination's value from governing claims stated in more than one
3673	notation of the same quantity; any session extending `parse_bound` or `compose_value`.
3674	ACTION: (1) Compose across notations, never within one. (2) Carry every notation the governing set
3675	states, and mark any notation the engine derived rather than read. (3) Mark a derived notation that
3676	does not terminate as inexact; never round it into the position of a stated figure. (4) This is a
3677	ruling about NOTATION of one quantity, not about UNITS: millimetres and degrees remain different
3678	units and the existing refusal to compose across them is untouched.
3679	DATE: 2026-09-17 — owner ruling, quoted above.
3680	
3681	## Owner ruling 2026-09-18 — UK is canonical; BE, ES, HR, IT and INT admitted to the jurisdiction enum
3682	
3683	> **"UK is canonical, add BE HR INT ES IT to the enum"**
3684	
3685	**WHAT THIS ANSWERS.** `JurisdictionCode` declared 27 codes while the corpus held eight the enum
3686	did not — so the declared vocabulary could not gate the column it described, and
3687	`governance/jurisdiction-philosophy.md`'s ERROR-level "GB rejected, must be UK" rule had **no gate on
3688	the database at all**: `validate_jurisdiction.py` globs source YAML and the standards registry and
3689	never reads a table. It passed with 0 errors over **27 GB rows across five tables**, two of which
3690	were written the same day.
3691	
3692	**WHAT IT SETTLES.**
3693	
3694	1. **UK, never GB**, confirmed. All 27 rows normalised;
3695	   `scripts/audit/jurisdiction_db_vocabulary.py` now enforces it on the DATABASE, deriving its table
3696	   list from the live schema and parsing the rejected spellings out of the philosophy document
3697	   rather than carrying a copy.
3698	2. **BE, ES, HR, IT, INT are admitted.** Each was already live in the CORPUS tables —
3699	   `evidence_sources`, `source_value_extractions`, `search_executions`, `research_code_leads`. With
3700	   them declared, every corpus jurisdiction value resolves, which is what makes the enum usable as a
3701	   gate.
3702	3. **INT is not ISO.** `ISO` means an ISO-published standard; `INT` means a work spanning
3703	   jurisdictions without being one — REF-00994 (IPC Accessibility Guide), REF-00977 (a review
3704	   searched across three databases). Both meta-codes, different meanings, recorded in the enum.
3705	
3706	**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the boundary is deliberate.** Roughly twenty further ISO codes are
3707	live in `lang_jur_map` — AR, AT, CL, CO, CR, CY, EC, ET, FI, GH, GT, MA, MX, PE, PH, PT, TH, TZ, UY.
3708	That table is a language-to-jurisdiction reference map of places the project **may expand into**, the
3709	"Phase 3 expansion" the validator warns about, not evidence it holds. They are **not** admitted here:
3710	admitting a code silently converts a candidate jurisdiction into a declared one, and that is a scope
3711	decision about the project's coverage rather than a vocabulary repair. The check exempts that table
3712	and says why.
3713	
3714	**TWO ANOMALIES SURFACED AND LEFT FOR A RULING**, in `term_aliases.jurisdiction`:
3715	`TW` (Taiwan — a real jurisdiction, undeclared, outside the five ruled on) and `colloquial` on
3716	TERM-027 *"place handicapé"* — **which is not a jurisdiction at all** but a register label written
3717	into the jurisdiction column. Reported by the check, non-blocking, because `term_aliases` is base
3718	vocabulary rather than admitted evidence and neither is this session's to decide.
3719	
3720	CONDITION: Any session admitting a source whose jurisdiction is not already declared; any session
3721	proposing an addition to `JurisdictionCode`.
3722	ACTION: (1) Derive what is live before proposing a code, and name WHICH tables carry it — corpus or
3723	reference. (2) Never write `GB`. (3) Do not admit a `lang_jur_map`-only code without a scope ruling.
3724	(4) `TW` and `colloquial` are owed a decision.
3725	DATE: 2026-09-18 — owner ruling, quoted above.
3726	
3727	## Owner ruling 2026-09-18 — EXECUTED IS `mined`; a deferral is legitimate so long as it eventually runs
3728	
3729	> **"executed is 'mined'"**
3730	>
3731	> and, immediately after:
3732	>
3733	> **"deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually"**
3734	
3735	Given in answer to batch 16's finding that `citation_mining.backward` and `.forward` are set to `1`
3736	by `log_mining` **unconditionally**, including on a deferral, so the direction flags do not
3737	distinguish a pass that ran from one that was logged. Recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0.
3738	
3739	**WHAT IT SETTLES, AND IT NARROWS THE DEFECT RATHER THAN WIDENING IT.**
3740	
3741	1. **The execution signal already exists and it is `evidence_sources.citation_mining_status`.**
3742	   `mined` means the pass ran; `deferred` means it did not. The column is live, it is populated, and
3743	   `log_mining` already derives it correctly (`deferred` with a reason, `mined` otherwise). Nothing
3744	   new needs building to answer "did this source get mined".
3745	2. **The direction columns are therefore not the home of that fact and must not be made one.**
3746	   Batch 16's proposed remedy — split `backward`/`forward` into attempted-versus-executed pairs —
3747	   is **refused by this ruling**: it would put one fact in a second home, which is rule 5, and the
3748	   first home already answers it. `backward=1` says a backward pass was *logged*; the status says
3749	   whether it *ran*. Read both.
3750	3. **A deferral is not a defect.** Depth-1 is a hard constraint (`citation-miner` §6) and a batch
3751	   that admits an anchor cannot mine it in the same pass. Deferring is the designed behaviour, and
3752	   batch 16's three new deferrals are correct.
3753	
3754	**WHAT REMAINS OWED, WHICH IS THE HALF THE RULING'S SECOND CLAUSE CREATES.** *"So long as it runs
3755	eventually"* is an obligation, and **nothing in this repository enforces it or even measures it**.
3756	There is no ageing on a deferred mining row, no backlog count, and no check that fails when a
3757	deferral goes unhonoured. A deferral that is never discharged is indistinguishable from one taken

## Owner ruling 2026-09-13 — the whole circulation corpus is untrusted and is cleared for a re-run

> **"I want you to clear all the recent research performed and how it went down the pipeline"**
>
> **"Basically all the circulation rows that have been produced are not able to be trusted, so we
> have to redo them all from the start"**

The second statement widened the first. "The recent research" read as batches 06 and 07; the ruling
is the whole slug. Executed as one compensating data migration
(`scripts/migrations/data_20260913040739_2026-09-13-clear-circulation-corpus.sql`, applied
2026-09-13 04:15) deleting **229 rows** — every row any stage produced under
`accessible-circulation-geometry`, reaching back through batches 04 and 05.

**The scope is the slug, not the sessions, and that distinction moved rows.** Deleting by session
stamp would have left 33 `observed_terms` that `session_2026-09-03-defect-programme` harvested from
circulation sources under its own name, and one `source_locators` row sitting in an 881-row table —
the row a re-run's R9 duplicate-DOI pre-check reads, so a stale locator for a deleted source is
exactly what makes a re-run cross-file against a `ref_id` that no longer exists.

**What was kept, and why none of it is research output.** `terms`, `term_aliases` and `slugs` are
base vocabulary minted 2026-05-09; TERM-001 `ramp gradient` and TERM-002 `corridor width` survive as
terms, while `base_parameters` — the *promotion* of those terms into the parameter layer — went, because
that promotion is research output. `research_code_leads` carries neither `ref_id` nor `slug`. The
acoustics corpus and `GAP-B01-*`/`GAP-B02-*` are out of scope. `retrieval-log/` is untouched on disk,
so a re-run verifies against the bytes the first run actually received and re-fetches nothing.
`sessions/` and `attestations/` stand as written: clearing rows is not erasing the audit trail.

**A CONSEQUENCE THE CLEAR CREATED AND DID NOT RESOLVE — read before the re-run.** Deleting the
thirteen circulation `ref_id`s dropped the global high-water mark from REF-00982 to REF-00970, because
the mark is the UNION over every `ref_id`-holding table (`dbcore.ref_id_high_water`) and only
`source_locators` still carries mintable ids. `dbcore.next_ref_id()` therefore returns **REF-00971** —
an identifier the batch-07 session record, its attestation, the retrieval-log manifests and PR #136 all
attribute to a different paper. A re-run will silently reuse REF-00971 … REF-00982 for new sources, and
`db.py`'s `_relation_quote_verified` searches *every* session's payloads with no structured `ref_id` in
the manifest, so a new REF-00971's quote can verify against the old REF-00971's bytes and read as
correct. `reference_stubs` is already in `ref_id_homes` and already carries a `RETIRED` status in its
CHECK, which makes it the obvious place to park the retired ids — but it was merged into
`source_locators` by migration 062 and has no writer, so reviving it is a decision, not a sweep.

**A second consequence, recorded not adjudicated.**
`decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md` records clause (c)'s freeze exit as
SATISFIED AND SPENT because `evidence_sources >= 1` was met, and `meta_work_freeze` was retired and
deleted on that basis. `evidence_sources` is 0 again. The DR says the freeze ended by its own terms, so
this is not a claim that it revives — but the condition that discharged it no longer holds and the gate
that could observe it no longer exists.

CONDITION: Any re-run of the `accessible-circulation-geometry` slug, or any future corpus clear.
ACTION: Settle the `ref_id` minting floor BEFORE admitting the first source, so retired identifiers are
not reissued. Derive the scope of any clear from the slug and its reachable `ref_id`s, never from
session stamps.
DATE: 2026-09-13 — owner ruling, quoted above. Recorded 2026-09-13 after an audit found the ruling
present in the migration, the session record and `governance/check-registry.yaml` but absent from this
ledger, which CLAUDE.md rule 0 requires ("Record the supersession").

---

RULE: **`AX-` may never denote an ICF code, anywhere.** Owner ruling 2026-09-13, quoted verbatim:
*"'AX-' for ICF should never ever exist anywhere."* Recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0.

**This answers the one question the `icf_demands` rename left open, and it answers it against the
status quo.** The 2026-08-25 RULE above renames `axes` → `icf_demands` and `axes.axis_code` →
`icf_demands.demand_code`, and the 2026-08-26 §R8 entry states that the rename "is SILENT on whether
the 17 **code values** are re-minted", that "the migration must state which", and that if they are not
re-minted then `AX-*` "stays correct live data" and belongs in the retired-vocabulary register's
`deferred:` section. It is now ruled: the values are re-minted. `AX-` is not correct live data.

**The surface, derived 2026-09-13 against the live database rather than quoted from the 2026-08-26
count, which predates the circulation clear.** 128 `AX-`-bearing values across fourteen columns:

| | |
|---|---|
| key columns | `population_axis_map.axis_code` 53 · `access_need_axis_map.axis_code` 21 · `axes.axis_code` 17 |
| free text | `terms.scope_note` 17 · `axes.falsification_condition` 8 · `access_need_icf.note` 3 · seven further columns 1 each |

Derive it, never quote it:

```
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3; con = sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
for (t,) in con.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='table' order by name"):
    for c in con.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")'):
        try: n = con.execute(f'select count(*) from "{t}" where "{c[1]}" GLOB "*AX-*"').fetchone()[0]
        except Exception: continue
        if n: print(f"{t}.{c[1]}: {n}")
PY
```

**WHERE THE RULING BITES HARDEST, and it is not the registry — it is four columns literally named
`icf_code`.** `specifications.icf_code`, `source_value_extractions.icf_code`,
`item_taxonomy_links.icf_code` and `icf_medical_map.icf_code` each carry a real FK into
`axes(axis_code)`, so the column called `icf_code` resolves, today, to an `AX-*` value. That is the
ruled state exactly: `AX-` denoting ICF, in the schema, four times over. Two further columns named
`icf_code` do NOT do this and must not be swept with them — `access_need_icf.icf_code` and
`population_icf_links.icf_code` (migration 080) hold real ICF codes and carry no FK into `axes`,
because there is no ICF registry to point at.

**What the ruling does NOT say, and must not be read to say.** It does not fold `icf_demands` into
`access_needs` — the 2026-08-25 RULE refuses that and its b/d ÷ e reasoning is untouched. It does not
retire the demand layer, whose rows anchor to ICF **b** and **d** codes in `icf_b_anchors` /
`icf_d_anchors`; those anchor columns are the layer's correct relationship to ICF and are not the
defect. And it does not license re-minting the 17 codes as bare ICF d-codes: an `icf_demands` row
anchors to both b and d codes, so no single d-code can stand for one, and collapsing the demand layer
into ICF would destroy the anchor relation the 2026-08-25 table sets out.

**TWO THINGS REMAIN UNDECIDED AND ARE NOT GUESSED HERE.** (1) The replacement code shape — `DM-AMB`
to match `demand_code` is the obvious reading and is still a minting decision every future row
carries. (2) Whether the four lens columns named `icf_code` are renamed to `demand_code` with the
registry, which would rename a LENS the owner ruled on 2026-08-28 (identity / ICF / access-need /
medical), or whether the ICF lens instead comes to hold real ICF codes and the demand layer becomes a
fifth thing. Those are put to the owner rather than settled by an implementer.

CONDITION: Any session writing, renaming or reasoning about the demand layer, the ICF lens, or any
column named `icf_code`; and any session about to add `AX-` to the retired-vocabulary register.
ACTION: (1) Write no new `AX-` value anywhere, under any column name. (2) Do not execute the re-mint
piecemeal — the 2026-08-25 RULE's action item 3 stands, and this ruling widens that migration rather
than replacing it. (3) When it runs, it states the new code shape and the lens-column decision
explicitly, because this ruling is what made both unavoidable. (4) The retired-vocabulary entry for
`AX-` still cannot be written in any of the register's three match modes — all require a non-`[\w-]`
character after the token, so `AX-` never matches `AX-AMB`; that is a matcher fact recorded on

`base_parameters.status = 'retired'`, `source_locators.status = 'RETIRED'`) … That is a doctrine
change and an owner decision, so it is named here and not smuggled in."* It is now made. Recorded on
contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0; the paperwork below is what the ruling CHANGES, never an argument
against it.

**WHAT IT SUPERSEDES.** 076's framing of the two floors as permanent; any future data migration that
hard-deletes rows to retract them; and `assess_cell`'s re-determination refusal keying on NOT EXISTS,
which the same comment says "could key on NOT RETIRED" under this rule — that is now the design, not
a hypothetical.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH, stated because the boundary is easy to over-read.** `CLAUDE.md` §8's
"Code, checks, scripts, dead tables and views: delete them" stands unchanged. This ruling governs
DATA ROWS AND IDENTIFIERS, where deleting destroys provenance the project cannot reconstruct. Git
history genuinely is the archive for code, so a deleted script loses nothing; a deleted row loses
the fact that it existed. The two are different objects and §8's removal-friendly posture on
apparatus is not weakened.

**WHY IT WAS RULED, in the owner's own framing:** *"This is a recurring provenance and data
management issue."* The floors 076 built are repairs applied after a delete has already destroyed
identity. They accumulate, and they collide: batch 08 found the thirteen RETIRED tombstones being
read as live DOI claims by BOTH `research_batch_dod.py` R9a and `db.py add-source`, so the re-run
the 2026-09-13 clearing ruling ordered could not admit a single cleared source by any route — the
only remedy either offered was to cross-file a retired identifier, which is the one thing 076 exists
to prevent. Both were fixed the same day by exempting RETIRED rows; neither fix would have been
needed had the rows never left.

flight when the ruling landed. Its strongest line: the views (`v_best_practice` and the rest) may not

ruling; it is a condition of executing it correctly. **No row is retired in place until every reader

## Owner statement 2026-09-16 — dose-response evidence may be reasoned to a range, AS A PROXY

> **"even if they aren't asserting a gradient, they are examining the impacts of gradients … this
> means that adjudication will be able to reason that whatever range of gradients corresponds to
> the best outcomes is the best range of gradient"**
>
> and, on being shown the limit of that inference:
>
> **"yes it's not perfect it's a proxy"**

**WHAT THIS SETTLES.** A source that measures the EFFECT of a parameter without prescribing a value
is not silent about that parameter, and judgment may reason from it toward a range. Batch 08 graded
four such sources and the engine returned `pending` with `refs=0`, which reads as "no evidence" over
two studies that measured articular discomfort rising 14→36% and pushrim force more than doubling.
That reading is wrong, and the mechanism is what makes it wrong: `assess_cell.gather_sources()`
gathers `figure_role IN ('claim','derived')` only, so a `finding` contributes nothing to a
determination however much it measured.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the limit is the owner's own word — PROXY.** The inference "best
outcomes therefore best range" has a degenerate solution on the evidence as it stands: both curves
are monotonic with no reported plateau, so "best" resolves to 0°, which is not a ramp. A ramp exists
to change level, so the design question is the MAXIMUM ACCEPTABLE gradient, and that needs a
threshold of acceptability which no admitted source supplies. Reasoning from dose-response to a
range is therefore a proxy step and must be marked as one, never recorded as though a source had
stated the value.

**THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS THE VOCABULARY FOR "PROXY" AND SHOULD USE IT HERE.**
`evidence_population_match.match_grade` carries PROXY for population-of-study vs population-served;
`source_value_extractions.value_directness` exists for how directly evidence bears on the claim and
sits at `NOT_ASSESSED` on every row because no grading rule has been ratified — which
`workplan/2026-09-10-road-to-batch-06.md` makes STOP CONDITION 4, "inventing one is a stop
condition". This statement is NOT read as ratifying a directness scale; it is read as ruling that
the proxy inference is ADMISSIBLE and must be MARKED. The scale itself is still owed.

**A LEAD THIS OPENS, recorded as a lead and not as a finding.** REF-00985 tested `0° to 4.8°`, and
`arctan(1/12) = 4.76°` — 1:12 being the ramp ceiling in ADA, AS 1428.1, BS 8300-1 and others. If
that ceiling is why 4.8° was chosen, the study measures discomfort across exactly the code-permitted
range and finds it climbing throughout, which under the 2026-09-13 ruling ("a finding that a CODE is
insufficient supplies no value, and is still first-class evidence") makes it a code-insufficiency
finding rather than a bare dose-response curve. THE ABSTRACT DOES NOT SAY THIS. It is an inference
from arithmetic and must be confirmed against the full text before it is filed as anything.

CONDITION: Any session determining a cell whose evidence measures effects rather than stating values;
any session implementing how `finding` rows reach a determination.
ACTION: (1) A determination may rest on dose-response findings, marked as a proxy, never as a stated
value. (2) `assess_cell` must be able to reach a determination from findings plus a threshold, not
only from `claim` rows — today it cannot, and that is why batch 08 reads `refs=0`. (3) The threshold
half is a code value or an equivalent criterion, and `research_code_leads` names which documents to
fetch but deliberately holds no values (2026-08-12 REFERENCE-ONLY ruling), so it must be retrieved.
(4) Do not invent a `value_directness` scale on the strength of this statement.

## Owner ruling 2026-09-17 — PRESENT BOTH notations; never choose between ratio and percentage

> **"Present both--don't choose between ratio or percentage."**

**WHAT THIS ANSWERS.** The `DEC` gap raised the same day by the ACTION (2) engine work. A gradient is
written as a ratio (`1:12`, `1:20`) by some sources and as a percentage (`5 %`, `6 %`) by others, and
they are the same physical quantity in two notations. `parse_bound` returns `None` for a ratio by
explicit design, so `compose_value` was building the determination's interval out of the
percentage-stated rows alone — measured on parameter 3: **2 of 7 governing claims**, with five rows
dropped. Migration 086 made that visible in `value_note` instead of silent. The question it left open
was whether the engine may convert, and the answer is that the question was malformed: **the engine
does not pick a notation at all. It presents both.**

**WHAT IT SETTLES.**

1. **No notation is dropped.** A governing claim stated as a ratio contributes to the determination on
   the same footing as one stated as a percentage. The 2-of-7 composition was a defect, not a policy.
2. **No notation is privileged.** The determination does not select a "canonical" form and relegate the
   other to a note. Both are carried, and a render surface shows both.
3. **Conversion is for COMPARISON, not for replacement.** The engine must compare across notations to
   apply the most-accommodating rule at all, and `1:20 = 5 %` exactly. That comparison is arithmetic.
   What it must not do is overwrite what a source wrote with the other form.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SETTLE, and the limit is arithmetic rather than doctrine.** Some conversions are
exact and some are not: `1:20` is exactly `5 %`, but `1:12` is `8.333…%` and no finite decimal is the
figure the source stated. So a derived notation is **marked as derived**, and where it does not
terminate it is marked as inexact as well. Presenting both does not license presenting a rounded
figure as though a source had written it — that is the 2026-08-19 shape, one column along.

**A CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING.** Until this ruling the engine's protection against inventing figures
was to refuse cross-unit composition outright, which cost it five of seven rows on the first cell it
determined. The protection was real and the cost was invisible. Both halves of that stay true and the
remedy is not to relax the refusal but to stop treating two notations of one quantity as two units.

CONDITION: Any session composing a determination's value from governing claims stated in more than one
notation of the same quantity; any session extending `parse_bound` or `compose_value`.
ACTION: (1) Compose across notations, never within one. (2) Carry every notation the governing set
states, and mark any notation the engine derived rather than read. (3) Mark a derived notation that
does not terminate as inexact; never round it into the position of a stated figure. (4) This is a
ruling about NOTATION of one quantity, not about UNITS: millimetres and degrees remain different
units and the existing refusal to compose across them is untouched.
DATE: 2026-09-17 — owner ruling, quoted above.

   new needs building to answer "did this source get mined".

eventually"* is an obligation, and **nothing in this repository enforces it or even measures it**.
There is no ageing on a deferred mining row, no backlog count, and no check that fails when a
deferral goes unhonoured. A deferral that is never discharged is indistinguishable from one taken

`citation_mining_completeness` counts **row presence**, so it reports deferrals as mined — measured
2026-09-18 at `10/10 T1-2 sources mined, 100.0%` repo-wide while the number of sources on
`accessible-circulation-geometry` whose backward pass had actually been executed was **3 of 13**.
Under this ruling that check is reading the wrong column: it must read `citation_mining_status`.
Derive both figures, never quote these:

**The snippet below derives BOTH quoted figures and nothing else.** The first version of it
derived neither — it printed a repo-wide tally across all tiers, so a reader told to re-derive
rather than trust got numbers that did not match the sentence above them. That is rule 7a's own
failure mode reappearing inside the remedy for it, and it is corrected here rather than excused.

```
python3 - <<'PY'
import sqlite3
con = sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
SLUG = 'accessible-circulation-geometry'

# FIGURE 1 -- what citation_mining_completeness reports: T1-2 sources with a mining ROW,
# over T1-2 sources in scope. It counts PRESENCE, which is the defect.
rows = con.execute("""
    select es.ref_id,
           (select count(*) from citation_mining c where c.global_ref_id = es.ref_id) has_row,
           es.citation_mining_status
    from evidence_sources es
    where es.tier in (1, 2)""").fetchall()
present = sum(1 for _, h, _ in rows if h)
print(f"as the check reports it : {present}/{len(rows)} T1-2 'mined' "
      f"= {100.0 * present / len(rows):.1f}%   <- PRESENCE, the overstatement")

# FIGURE 2 -- what actually ran on the slug: status='mined' is the execution signal.
slug_rows = con.execute("""
    select es.citation_mining_status
    from evidence_sources es
    join source_slug_links l on l.ref_id = es.ref_id
    where l.slug = ? and exists
          (select 1 from citation_mining c
            where c.global_ref_id = es.ref_id and c.slug = l.slug)""", (SLUG,)).fetchall()
executed = sum(1 for (st,) in slug_rows if st == 'mined')
print(f"as execution reports it : {executed} of {len(slug_rows)} on {SLUG}")

for st in ('mined', 'deferred', 'pending'):
    n = con.execute("select count(*) from evidence_sources "
                    "where citation_mining_status = ?", (st,)).fetchone()[0]
    print(f"  corpus-wide {st:<9}: {n}")
PY
```

weighing its tier. Recorded per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0, and it **overrides the tier the ladder would
otherwise have produced on study design alone.**

**WHAT IT SETTLES, AND IT CUTS AGAINST THE ADMITTING SESSION'S OWN INCLINATION.** On
`governance/tier-system.md` §1 read mechanically, the study is a candidate for
`clinical`/`high_control` → **T1**: the parameter under design was experimentally manipulated (a
purpose-built 40-ft ramp reset from 1:12 to 1:16 to 1:20), the outcome was physiological (pulse
recovery to within ten beats of resting), and n = 124 disabled participants. That is the T1
definition on its face, and it is the reading this session was about to take.

**The ruling refuses it, and the refusal is about CURRENCY rather than about design quality.** A
determination is a statement about what to build **now**. A 1979 measurement was taken on 1979
wheelchairs, by people trained in 1979 rehabilitation practice, against 1979 expectations of what a
disabled person should have to tolerate — and the anchoring band (T1 / Co-1 / T2 / Co-2) is the band
the guidebook uses to say *this is best practice today*. Historical distance is not a defect in the
study; it is a mismatch between the study and the claim it would be made to anchor.

**HOW IT IS EXPRESSED IN THE SCHEMA.** `evidence_type='grey'`, `scope='intrinsic'` → **T3**, marker
**○**, which `tier-system.md` §1 glosses as *"Supporting evidence for best-practice claims; rarely
the sole basis"* — precisely "grounding, not standard". The study-design facts are not discarded:
they are recorded in `verification_note` and in the extractions, so a later session can see that a
high-control design was admitted at T3 **by ruling** and not by anyone mistaking its methods.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY.** It does not retire the source, does not make its findings false, and does
not bar it from a determination's supporting set. It bars it from being the **anchor**. Nor is this
a general rule that old work is weak: it is a ruling about 1979 work being used to state a
present-day building parameter. Where the claim is itself historical — *what did the evidence say
when this code was written* — this source is **primary and first-class**, and that is the use batch
18 makes of it.

**AND IT LEAVES THE REAL BLOCKER EXACTLY WHERE IT WAS.** Parameter 3 × MOB stays undetermined,
determination gate 1 stays open, and C10 still refuses (GAP-020, GAP-024). This ruling means batch
18 did not move that, and the batch's own pre-registered prior P3 predicted it would not.

CONDITION: Any session admitting a source published before roughly 1990, or weighing an old but
methodologically strong study for an anchoring tier.
ACTION: (1) Age is a CURRENCY judgement, made separately from study design — do not let a strong
method carry an old source into the anchoring band. (2) Record the design facts anyway, so the T3 is
legible as a ruling rather than as a misreading. (3) Historical-provenance claims are a different
claim type, and old primary work anchors those at full strength.

## Owner rulings 2026-09-26 — `results_admitted` is raise-only after insert; a proxy provenance edge is repaired before merge

Given on PR #159 (research batch 20) and relayed by the coordinating session, so recorded here in
that session's words rather than as quotations. Recorded on contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0. Full
record: `sessions/session_2026-09-25-research-batch-20-audit-cluster-templer-fhwa.md`, §0c–§0d.

**(1) `search_executions.results_admitted` IS RAISE-ONLY AFTER INSERT.**
- `log-search` sets the count from the search's own edges at insert.
- An admission edge added later to that search (`db.py link-admission`) raises the count to
  max(count, edges).
- Removing a wrong edge (`db.py unlink-admission`) lowers it by one, never below the edges that
  remain.
- **The count is never lowered to force agreement with the edges.**

The rule was first written by a session as a reconciliation of two records that disagreed. The
owner confirmed it as the answer, not a stopgap.

**What it supersedes, for post-insert writes:**
- `DR-2026-08-19` step 7's "the count must agree exactly".
- The 2026-09-02 repair's "nothing updates it thereafter" (the H05 note in
  `scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py`, which now carries an appended pointer here).

**What it keeps:** that repair's lesson. H05 stays deleted, no parity check returns, and the
historical counts restored above their edges stay as they are. The rule's one home is
`_results_admitted_after` in `scripts/db.py`. GAP-051 is closed as decided.

**(2) A PROXY PROVENANCE EDGE IS REPAIRED, NOT MERGED.** Batch 20's two admission edges copied
candidate rows that batch 19 had filed on the nearest logged search, because the steps that
actually surfaced them were never logged. The ruling was to fix it before merge, on batch 17's
precedent (candidates 107/108):
1. log each real discovery step as a backfill search (`log-search --backfill 1`, a prior that
   states its own absence, and a `query_text` that says honestly what was done);
2. move the candidates with `reattribute-candidate`;
3. move the edges with `unlink-admission` and `link-admission`.

An ad hoc lookup is logged as what it was, not dressed as a designed query. GAP-050 records the
chain.

CONDITION: any session that writes, moves or audits an admission edge on a search that is
already logged, or finds a candidate filed on a search that did not surface it.
ACTION:
1. Never lower `results_admitted` to meet the edges; let the two verbs move it.
2. When a candidate's search is a proxy, backfill the real step and move the candidate and its
   edge. Never leave the proxy in place, and never re-describe the proxy search as the source.

(3) Answer the synthesis-floor question by class: Opus-class or above, which includes Fable-class. (4) Do not re-pin the floor to whatever model is current — that recreates the defect.

608	RULE: A parameter and its element are distinct terms; a relation between concepts is a pointer, never a shared alias string. The controlled vocabulary (`terms`/`term_aliases`/`term_item_links`) had been built parameter-first — `corridor width` with no `corridor`, reverberation time and sound masking with nothing for absorption — so equivalent wordings could not group and 38 of 106 slugs resolved to no vocabulary at all. Both layers now exist and each `scope_note` names its counterpart: TERM-002 (corridor width) ↔ TERM-048 (circulation route); TERM-012 (sensory room, the designated facility) ↔ TERM-074 (withdrawal space, the wider provision); TERM-016 (wheelchair user, the person) ↔ TERM-079 (mobility aid, the equipment). The pointer rule was earned: TERM-074 was first authored claiming `quiet room` and its equivalents in thirteen languages — strings TERM-012 already owned. **Two concepts sharing an alias is not a link; it is a collision that makes retrieval ambiguous and the register self-contradictory.** Deliberate exception: population/project codes (OFS, TALL, LMB, MOVE) may map to two sibling concepts because searching the code should return both — those rows are annotated as intentional so a later audit reads them as intent, not drift. Paired decision: DR-2026-07-25-controlled-vocabulary-grouping-and-provenance §2.
609	CONDITION: Any session adding, renaming, or merging entries in `terms`/`term_aliases`, or reasoning about why a search returned the wrong concept.
610	ACTION: (1) When adding a dimensional parameter, check whether its element exists, and vice versa. (2) Never express a relation by giving two terms the same alias — use NARROWER/BROADER and name the counterpart in `scope_note`. (3) Run `python3 scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py` and the collision query AFTER the change, not only before. (4) Annotate any deliberate shared code alias as deliberate.
611	DATE: 2026-07-25 — owner request ("build a list of synonyms across each language ... ensure that equivalent words for a term get grouped")

614	RULE: Match slug tokens, never substrings — and re-run the audit AFTER the change. `scripts/generate_search_queries.py` resolved a slug to terms with `lower(canonical_en) LIKE '%<slug word>%'`. That is a substring search wearing a synonym lookup's clothes, and it had been silently mis-matching: `room`→head**room**, `ot`→vibr**ot**actile, `aut`→dys**aut**onomia, `read`→adaptable **Read**iness, `and`→every canonical containing the word. **Invisible because the generator prints queries, not the terms behind them** — the apparatus reported coverage it did not have. Replaced by token matching over canonical names AND English aliases (so the synonym chart drives retrieval), plus a corpus-derived stoplist (`environment` appears in 31 of 106 slugs, `built` 30, `design` 19 — no discriminating power) and a specificity rule that discards common-token-only matches when a rare token also matched. Coverage 68/106 → 106/106; matches per slug from a 12-match maximum to a mean of 1.8. Two hazards recorded because they are characteristic of this repair: (a) a naive stemmer must not strip the final `s` of *access*/*cross*/*analysis* — an earlier version produced `acces` and `cros`, a NEW false-positive class introduced by the fix for the old one; (b) when a synonym causes a bad match the SYNONYM is the defect — six aliases were reworded (`resting place` collided with "Changing **Places**") rather than widening the stoplist, which would suppress the signal everywhere else. Paired decision: DR-2026-07-25-controlled-vocabulary-grouping-and-provenance §3.
615	CONDITION: Any session changing slug→term resolution, adding controlled vocabulary, or investigating why a generated search query contains an unrelated term.
616	ACTION: (1) Never resolve an identifier by substring against a name; tokenise both sides. (2) Print the TERMS a slug resolved to, not only the query, when checking retrieval. (3) After changing vocabulary, re-run the false-positive sweep across ALL slugs — a check run only before the change cannot fail. (4) Fix the offending alias, not the stoplist, when one synonym causes the bad match.
617	DATE: 2026-07-25

619	
620	RULE: An alias declares its provenance; unlabelled is worse than labelled-unverified. `term_aliases` drives multilingual retrieval, but nothing recorded where a term came from: 881 aliases carried no marker, 789 of them non-English, so a reader could not tell a national-standards-glossary term from a model-generated one. This is a trust problem, not a formatting one — **a wrong search term returns zero results indistinguishably from an absent literature**, so the apparatus cannot tell you it searched with the wrong word. Every alias created on or after 2026-07-24 must carry a provenance marker in `notes`; earlier cohorts are grandfathered and reported (backfill-on-touch, as with attestations) rather than blocking work on 880 retro-documentations. Markers adopt `references/native-alias-verification.md` rather than a parallel vocabulary, so MODEL-GENERATED has a defined exit: → VERIFIED-GLOSSARY (standards-body glossary) / VERIFIED-NATIVE (qualified native-speaker review) / VERIFIED-CROSS (corroborated across published sources). Enforcement level 4 (`scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py`, blocking in `audit.yml`); it failed a row written earlier in the same session on its first run, which is the point. **Do not model-generate vocabulary in a language nobody on the project reads** — no one here could detect a wrong term, so the claim is unfalsifiable by construction; source it from a published glossary or register the gap (GAP-302). Standing state as of the 2026-07-25 merge: 15 aliases (Indonesian, VERIFIED-GLOSSARY against Permen PUPR 14/2017 and UU 8/2016) are verified; 2367 are not (GAP-303). That Indonesian build is the worked example of the remedy — named national instrument, verbatim retrieval, no back-translation — and it also exposed the gate's own defect: provenance asserted in PROSE failed a marker-string check, i.e. the gate blocked the best work in the register while passing generated work. **A convention introduced mid-flight meets correct work that predates it, and the convention is what yields.** Paired decision: DR-2026-07-25-controlled-vocabulary-grouping-and-provenance §4, §6.
621	CONDITION: Any session adding or editing `term_aliases`, generating search vocabulary, or assessing how far to trust a non-English retrieval result.
622	ACTION: (1) Record a provenance marker on every alias you add. (2) Flag model-generated terms as such and say so in any artefact that ships them. (3) Never invent controlled vocabulary in a language you cannot read — register a gap naming the glossary to source it from. (4) Treat non-English retrieval as unverified until a VERIFIED-* marker exists; do not report its coverage as if confirmed.
623	DATE: 2026-07-25 — owner directive ("did we fix everything identified?", then "resolve usefully")

626	RULE: An environment contract is enforced or it is fiction — and an exemption declares what it depends on. `CLAUDE.md` §7 stated "Every DB-aware script honours `GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH`". It was false for 9 of the live DB-connecting scripts, and it cost real work: a reach test pointed at a scratch copy silently read the committed database and reported "no change" for a change that had taken effect. Fixed in all 9 and promoted to level 4 via `scripts/audit/db_path_env_audit.py` (blocking in `audit.yml`, where steps set the variable explicitly, so a script ignoring it reads whatever is on disk rather than what CI intended). Scope is found by AST — calls `sqlite3.connect` AND names the DB outside a docstring, so prose mentions do not count — over `scripts/`+`tools/` minus the one-time/legacy dirs, using the same `EXCLUDE_PARTS` as the code-layer audit so "legacy" means one thing repo-wide. **Note `scripts/db/**` targets `data/db/guidebook.db`, a DIFFERENT legacy file that is not the canonical database.** Two exemptions are documented in the script rather than silent, and the delegating one declares `delegates_to` so it SELF-INVALIDATES: if `graph/build.py` ever stops honouring the variable, `graph_audit.py`'s exemption reports STALE and the audit fails rather than covering for it. Paired decision: DR-2026-07-25-controlled-vocabulary-grouping-and-provenance §5.

628	ACTION: (1) Resolve the DB path as `Path(os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", <default>))`. (2) Before trusting a test that redirects the DB, confirm the script under test honours the variable. (3) An exemption states its reason in the audit and, where it rests on another component, names that component so the exemption dies with it. (4) When a documented contract turns out to be false, fix the code AND the document — and gate it, so the claim cannot silently rot again.
629	DATE: 2026-07-25 — owner directive ("We MUST resolve this")

631	
632	RULE: Search for the existing work before writing anything — code, check, register, plan or rule. This repository re-derives its own conclusions faster than it acts on them, and the cost is not wasted effort but *false novelty*: a conclusion reached twice reads as confirmation when it is actually evidence that the first one was never executed. The rule was earned on 2026-08-19, when a session proposed a "meta-work freeze" as a new idea and then found `workplan/next-steps-synthesis-2026-07-14.md` §2.6 had already declared one — *"Governance freeze for the duration. No new DR / adversarial pass / attestation cycle unless it demonstrably blocks a synthesis slug"* — carrying a mechanical tripwire at §3: *"If a week passes with `reasoning_doc_citations` unchanged and any governance commit landed, the freeze was breached — stop and re-read this section."* Measured that day: five weeks elapsed, `reasoning_doc_citations` still 0 rows, and 60 Decision Records, 87 attestations and 140 workplan documents added since the freeze was declared. The tripwire's firing condition had been met every week for five weeks and no session had checked it. The same session also re-derived, independently and without citation, at least four conclusions the repo had already recorded elsewhere. **A rule nobody re-reads is indistinguishable from a rule nobody wrote** — so the check must happen before the work, not in review, because by review time the duplicate already exists and arguing it away costs more than it saved. The failure mode this prevents is not duplicated code; it is a repository that mistakes its own echo for progress.
633	CONDITION: Before writing any script, check, registry entry, workplan document, decision record, standing rule, register, sweep or protocol — and before proposing one. Also whenever a finding feels novel: novelty is the signal to search, not to write.
634	ACTION: (1) Search first and say what you searched: `governance/check-registry.yaml` and `references/tooling-register.md` for an existing check or tool; `scripts/` and `tools/` by function, not by filename, for existing code; `references/project-standards.md` for a live rule; `decisions/` and the `decisions` table for a prior ruling; `workplan/` sorted by date for a prior plan. Remember the root `.ignore` hides `_archived/`, `audits/`, `sessions/`, `workplan/_superseded/` and `versions/` from ripgrep — search those by explicit path or the answer will be a false negative. (2) If prior work exists, extend or cite it; do not restate it. If you supersede it, say what changed and why the earlier version failed. (3) If a prior rule, freeze or tripwire covers your situation, check whether it was ever executed before proposing its replacement — an unenforced rule needs teeth, not a successor. (4) Record the search in the session record or the artifact itself, so the next session inherits the negative result and does not repeat it. A search that found nothing is a completed unit of work, exactly as R8 says of a zero-yield literature search.
635	DATE: 2026-08-19 — owner directive ("add a standing rule to always check for existing work/tools before writing any code")
636	
637	
638	RULE: Adversarial review is a truth-instrument bound to evidence, never a plan-instrument. An adversarial pass may be commissioned ONLY against a diff that (a) wrote rows to the research tables (`search_executions`, `search_candidates`, `evidence_sources`, `source_slug_links`, `evidence_population_match`, `source_value_extractions`, `specifications`, `convergence_assessment`, `jurisdictional_values`, `case_studies`, `economics_entries`) or (b) authored or amended a synthesis artifact (`references/bpc-reasoning/*`, `best_practice_synthesis`, a rendered determination page). Plans, critiques, censuses, handoffs, registers, session records, Decision Records and this ledger are not adversarial-pass subjects; they receive the mechanical gates already registered and nothing more. The rule was earned by measurement: **at least ten fresh-context adversarial passes ran between 2026-07-14 and 2026-08-19, and not one examined research output**, because there is none — every research table stands at zero rows. The fresh-session independence convention (`workplan/2026-08-15-adversarial-brief-pr103.md` §0, "Run this in fresh context. Do not read the authoring session's reasoning first") is epistemically correct AND is the mechanism guaranteeing a new session per critique, so critique → plan → critique became the tightest loop in the repository. The one counter-example is the standard to copy: `sessions/session_2026-07-26-energy-conservation-rest-points-seating-adversarial.md`, the only pass ever run on research output, produced **seven sustained findings in a single session**, all against the author's own admitted batch, catching error in both directions — a T1-candidate under-tiered at T3 and a no-participants discussion piece over-tiered, plus one dataset admitted twice under two ref_ids and a circular value. Its own diagnosis is the thing this rule protects: *"a claim pitched at a confidence the retrieval didn't earn."* **The agonist needs no construction: R1-R15 already compel the authoring session to file its complete affirmative case as rows.** The antagonist attacks that recorded case through named lenses — existence, fidelity, independence, tier, population, contrary-finding, recognition by the population served, and query-shape — and the cheapest agonist-antagonist mechanic is blind-then-compare: re-grade tier and population-match independently BEFORE seeing the author's grades, then diff. A pass whose subject is a plan cannot be wrong about anything a reader could check.
639	CONDITION: Any proposal — by owner prompt, session initiative, plan clause, or a prior pass's own finding — to run an "adversarial pass", "critique", "cold review", or fresh-session audit of any artifact.
640	ACTION: (1) Test the target against (a)/(b). If it fails, decline in one line of the session log; no critique document may be written. (2) A qualifying pass records each finding as claim-attacked / method / verdict / severity, and records SURVIVED claims as well as SUSTAINED ones — a zero-finding pass must be able to show what it attacked, or it is indistinguishable from a pass that never ran. (3) Close each sustained finding by row correction, in the same pass, via migration; where the authoring session disputes it, cap the affected cell at `provisional` and record the dispute. Never schedule remediation — a pass emits data plus one session record, and may not create or modify a workplan. (4) To contest a plan, append a single objection of at most one page to the plan file itself, naming the clause and the evidence, and flag the owner. No standalone contest document, and no counter-critique of the objection. (5) Budget: at most one adversarial pass per research batch. A pass on a pass is forbidden — defects in a pass are the next batch's pass's business.
641	DATE: 2026-08-19 — owner directive ("the plan will require adversarial reviews to ensure accuracy and factuality, and it may need to be agonist-antagonist in manner")

RULE: Work from axes — no armchair umbrellas. All population/profile curation, demand-mapping, and specification proceeds FROM the functional axes (Layer 1 of the two-layer taxonomy, `governance/functional-taxonomy.md`) — the specific, architect-actionable, diagnosis-neutral, co-occurrence-native demand dimensions — never FROM broad population/profile umbrellas. The profile layer (Layer 2) is populated only with specific self-identified communities named on their own terms (co-produced; "nothing about us without us"); it is never a place to coin lumped coalition codes from an armchair. Broad umbrellas ("physically disabled"; clinical-cluster relabels like "energy-limiting chronic illness") are forbidden as profile codes: they collapse opposed and orthogonal design demands and erase specific communities — the pre-taxonomy category-thinking that §1.3, the irreducibility principle (functional-taxonomy §0.5), and mapping-confidence (§3.2) exist to end. A population is a mapping-confidence-weighted vector over axes, not a bucket. Umbrellas may exist only as additive cross-cutting tags over specifics, never as replacement codes. Provenance: three self-caught erasures in session 2026-07-21/22 — OFS→"ELCI" erased POTS (orthostatic/autonomic) + ME (exertional) + MCAS (chemical/immune), three distinct axis signatures; respiratory/pulmonary dismissed as "decomposed" (dyspnea ≠ fatigue ≠ chemical); "physically disabled/wheelchair users" erased the ambulatory and part-time-wheelchair disabled and buried the orthogonal upper-limb/reach axis. In each case the axis layer already held the distinctions the umbrella destroyed. Paired decision: DR-2026-07-22-work-from-axes.

RULE: Merge implies ratification. When the owner merges a branch/PR to `main`, that act ratifies every decision, Decision Record, governance proposal, and rule-change the merge contains — with the same force as an explicit "ratify" directive — UNLESS the owner explicitly notes otherwise on that merge (e.g. "merging to iterate, not ratified", "staged only"). Scope and limits: (1) merge ratifies the DECISION; it does not by itself COMPLETE staged/deferred EXECUTION a DR gates behind ratification — those items become authorized-and-owed, tracked in the ratification-execution register, not silently done. (2) It does not waive genuine external preconditions a DR names (e.g. an owner-only input like the deployed `<audit_trail>` list, or a doctrine-SHA-cascade edit requiring the materiality triage) — those remain real work, now authorized. (3) It does not convert an evidence-maturity `provisional`/`pending` cell or BPC to `stated`; evidence state is governed by evidence strength, not ratification. (4) DG-NON items still require the owner's substantive direction to have occurred — merge ratifies what the owner decided, it does not manufacture a decision the owner never made. (4) Do not use this rule to auto-complete DG-NON substance the owner never decided, to skip named external preconditions, or to promote evidence-maturity states.

RULE: A rendered document is a derived surface — gate it, do not re-read it. A hand-authored rendered document (`specs/*.html` and any successor surface) may SUMMARISE the canonical record; it may NOT contradict it, and it may NOT present it as stronger than it is. Provenance: session 2026-07-24/25 built the E-08 corridor-width prototype and put it through three independent adversarial audits (machine vision at four viewports; contemporary design/UX; four role perspectives — design catalogue, lived experience/advocate, policymaker research, OT consultant). RULE: Search for the existing work before writing anything — code, check, register, plan or rule. RULE: Adversarial review is a truth-instrument bound to evidence, never a plan-instrument. An adversarial pass may be commissioned ONLY against a diff that (a) wrote rows to the research tables (`search_executions`, `search_candidates`, `evidence_sources`, `source_slug_links`, `evidence_population_match`, `source_value_extractions`, `specifications`, `convergence_assessment`, `jurisdictional_values`, `case_studies`, `economics_entries`) or (b) authored or amended a synthesis artifact (`references/bpc-reasoning/*`, `best_practice_synthesis`, a rendered determination page). Plans, critiques, censuses, handoffs, registers, session records, Decision Records and this ledger are not adversarial-pass subjects; they receive the mechanical gates already registered and nothing more. The rule was earned by measurement: **at least ten fresh-context adversarial passes ran between 2026-07-14 and 2026-08-19, and not one examined research output**, because there is none — every research table stands at zero rows. The fresh-session independence convention (`workplan/2026-08-15-adversarial-brief-pr103.md` §0, "Run this in fresh context. Do not read the authoring session's reasoning first") is epistemically correct AND is the mechanism guaranteeing a new session per critique, so critique → plan → critique became the tightest loop in the repository. The one counter-example is the standard to copy: `sessions/session_2026-07-26-energy-conservation-rest-points-seating-adversarial.md`, the only pass ever run on research output, produced **seven sustained findings in a single session**, all against the author's own admitted batch, catching error in both directions — a T1-candidate under-tiered at T3 and a no-participants discussion piece over-tiered, plus one dataset admitted twice under two ref_ids and a circular value. Its own diagnosis is the thing this rule protects: *"a claim pitched at a confidence the retrieval didn't earn."* **The agonist needs no construction: R1-R15 already compel the authoring session to file its complete affirmative case as rows.** The antagonist attacks that recorded case through named lenses — existence, fidelity, independence, tier, population, contrary-finding, recognition by the population served, and query-shape — and the cheapest agonist-antagonist mechanic is blind-then-compare: re-grade tier and population-match independently BEFORE seeing the author's grades, then diff. A pass whose subject is a plan cannot be wrong about anything a reader could check.
CONDITION: Any proposal — by owner prompt, session initiative, plan clause, or a prior pass's own finding — to run an "adversarial pass", "critique", "cold review", or fresh-session audit of any artifact.
ACTION: (1) Test the target against (a)/(b). If it fails, decline in one line of the session log; no critique document may be written. (2) A qualifying pass records each finding as claim-attacked / method / verdict / severity, and records SURVIVED claims as well as SUSTAINED ones — a zero-finding pass must be able to show what it attacked, or it is indistinguishable from a pass that never ran. You are extracting NORMATIVE ATOMS from project documents. Read-only: do not edit anything under /home/user; write only to the output path below. Purpose: flatten the owner's active rulings and the project's operative rules into atomic, individually testable statements so conflicts between them can later be found mechanically. You do NOT adjudicate conflicts; you extract faithfully and flag what looks inconsistent.

REPO: /home/user/guidebook. Use the Read tool to read files (the Grep tool and ripgrep are blinded to sessions/, audits/, _archived/ by .ignore; to search use `grep -rn` in Bash).

ASSIGNED FILES (read every one IN FULL, in chunks with offset/limit; do not skim, do not stop at headings):
  governance/tier-system.md
  governance/evidence-architecture.md
  governance/evidence-methodology.md
OUTPUT: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/db856d85-2082-5d35-9529-aa996506261b/scratchpad/graph/atoms-evi.jsonl   (id prefix EVI-)

ATOM = one JSON object per line:
{"id":"EVI-001","source":"governance/tier-system.md:42","quote":"<exact contiguous substring of the file, <=300 chars, keep markdown emphasis characters>","modality":"MUST|MUST_NOT|MAY|DEFINES|CARDINALITY|ORDER|EQUATES|RESERVES|OPEN","subject":"short noun phrase","claim":"ONE sentence, atomic: a single testable obligation, prohibition, permission, definition, cardinality, ordering, equation, reservation or open question","scope":{"stages":["base|research|evidence|judgment|synthesis|specification|render|cross"],"objects":["tables/columns/verbs/scripts/files/checks the TEXT names"]},"speaker":"OWNER_QUOTED|OWNER_RELAYED|RATIFIED_DOC|AGENT_PROPOSAL|PROCESS_RULE","date":"YYYY-MM-DD or null","status":"ACTIVE|SUPERSEDED|AMENDED|PROPOSED|OPEN|HISTORICAL","status_evidence":"exact substring of the file that marks it superseded/amended/proposed/open, or null","superseded_by":"free-text pointer or null","enforcement":"the check/verb/constraint the TEXT says enforces it, 'NOT ENFORCED' if it says so, else null","ambiguity":"null or one sentence if the text reads two ways"}

RULES
1. One atom per distinct obligation/prohibition/permission/definition/cardinality/order/equation/reservation/open question. Split compound sentences when the parts can fail independently.
2. Operative content only. Skip history, measurements, rationale, worked examples, unless they state a rule. Keep a number only if the document makes it a rule; then put the number in the claim.
3. quote must be an exact copy (verifier checks it); source line = line where the quote starts.
4. status ACTIVE unless the document itself marks the text superseded/amended/proposed/open/historical; then set status and quote the marking in status_evidence.
5. speaker: OWNER_QUOTED only when the quote is the owner's own words in quotation marks attributed to the owner; OWNER_RELAYED when the document reports an owner decision in its own words; RATIFIED_DOC for text of a ratified/canonical document; AGENT_PROPOSAL for PROPOSED or agent-authored design; PROCESS_RULE for how work is done (workflow, gates, commits) rather than what the data/pipeline is.
6. Do not invent. If unsure of a field, use null.
7. When finished, run: python3 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/db856d85-2082-5d35-9529-aa996506261b/scratchpad/graph/verify_atoms.py <your output file>  — fix every reported failure (re-copy the quote from the file) and re-run until it prints 0 problem(s).

RETURN (short): atom counts by status and by modality; up to 15 lines "TENSION NOTICED: <atom ids> — why" for statements within or across the files you read that appear to contradict or fit uneasily (flag only, do not resolve); and anything you could not read or finish.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resolve hand-authored atoms (quote + file, no line number) to file:line and write JSONL.
usage: build_atoms.py authored_X.py out.jsonl     (authored_X.py defines ATOMS = [A(...), ...])
A quote that cannot be found verbatim is reported and the atom is NOT written."""
import json, re, sys, importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
REPO = Path("/home/user/guidebook")

def A(i, f, q, mod, subj, claim, st, obj=(), spk="RATIFIED_DOC", date=None, status="ACTIVE",
      ev=None, by=None, enf=None, amb=None, **extra):
    return dict(id=i, file=f, quote=q, modality=mod, subject=subj, claim=claim,
                scope={"stages": list(st.split("|")) if isinstance(st, str) else list(st), "objects": list(obj)},
                speaker=spk, date=date, status=status, status_evidence=ev, superseded_by=by,
                enforcement=enf, ambiguity=amb, **extra)

_norm_cache = {}
def index(path):
    if path in _norm_cache: return _norm_cache[path]
    lines = (REPO / path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").split("\n")
    buf, starts = [], []          # normalised text, and line number per char
    out_chars, out_lines = [], []
    for n, ln in enumerate(lines, 1):
        ln = re.sub(r"^\s*>\s?", "", ln)
        for tok in re.split(r"(\s+)", ln):
            if not tok: continue
            if tok.isspace(): ch = " "
            else: ch = tok
            out_chars.append(ch); out_lines.extend([n] * len(ch))
        out_chars.append(" "); out_lines.append(n)
    text = "".join(out_chars)
    text = re.sub(r" +", lambda m: " ", text)   # collapse (line map rebuilt below)
    # rebuild map after collapsing
    chars, lmap, prev_space = [], [], False
    for c, n in zip("".join(out_chars), out_lines):
        if c == " ":
            if prev_space: continue
            prev_space = True
        else:
            prev_space = False
        chars.append(c); lmap.append(n)
    _norm_cache[path] = ("".join(chars), lmap)
    return _norm_cache[path]

def resolve(a):
    t, lmap = index(a["file"])
    q = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", re.sub(r"^\s*>\s?", "", a["quote"])).strip()
    k = t.find(q)
    if k < 0: return None
    cnt = t.count(q)
    a = dict(a); a["source"] = f"{a['file']}:{lmap[k]}"; a["quote_occurrences"] = cnt
    del a["file"]
    return a

if __name__ == "__main__":
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("auth", sys.argv[1]); m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules["auth"] = m
    m.A = A
    spec.loader.exec_module(m)
    ok = bad = 0
    with open(sys.argv[2], "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for a in m.ATOMS:
            r = resolve(a)
            if r is None:
                print(f"{a['id']}: QUOTE NOT FOUND in {a['file']}: {a['quote'][:80]!r}"); bad += 1; continue
            fh.write(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"); ok += 1
    print(f"{ok} written, {bad} unresolved")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Derive schema facts for the state graph. usage: probe_schema.py REPO_ROOT OUT.json  (read-only on the DB)"""
import json, re, sqlite3, sys, yaml
from pathlib import Path
repo = Path(sys.argv[1]); out = sys.argv[2]
con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{repo}/data/guidebook.db?mode=ro", uri=True)
uv = con.execute("pragma user_version").fetchone()[0]
stagemap = yaml.safe_load(open(repo / "governance/stage-map.yaml"))
contract = yaml.safe_load(open(repo / "governance/pipeline-contract.yaml"))
stages = [s["id"] for s in contract["stages"]]
tables = [r[0] for r in con.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type='table' and name not like 'sqlite_%' order by 1")]
views = {r[0]: r[1] for r in con.execute("select name, sql from sqlite_master where type='view' order by 1")}
rows = {t: con.execute(f'select count(*) from "{t}"').fetchone()[0] for t in tables}
sm = stagemap["tables"]
res = {"user_version": uv, "stages": stages, "n_tables": len(tables), "n_views": len(views)}
res["in_schema_not_in_stage_map"] = sorted(set(tables) - set(sm))
res["in_stage_map_not_in_schema"] = sorted(set(sm) - set(tables))
res["stage_ids_unknown"] = sorted({v for v in sm.values() if v not in stages and v != "infrastructure"})
# FK graph
fks = []
for t in tables:
    for f in con.execute(f'pragma foreign_key_list("{t}")'):
        notnull = {c[1]: c[3] for c in con.execute(f'pragma table_info("{t}")')}.get(f[3], 0)
        fks.append({"child": t, "col": f[3], "parent": f[2], "pcol": f[4], "notnull": bool(notnull)})
res["fks"] = fks
empty = {t for t, n in rows.items() if n == 0}
res["empty_tables"] = sorted(empty)
res["unwritable"] = sorted({f"{f['child']}.{f['col']} -> {f['parent']}" for f in fks if f["parent"] in empty and f["notnull"]})
# stage of each table; cross-stage FKs
def st(t): return sm.get(t, "?")
cross = [f for f in fks if st(f["child"]) != st(f["parent"]) and "infrastructure" not in (st(f["child"]), st(f["parent"]))]
res["cross_stage_fk_count"] = len(cross)
# CHECK vocabularies
vocab = {}
for t in tables:
    ddl = con.execute("select sql from sqlite_master where name=?", (t,)).fetchone()[0] or ""
    for m in re.finditer(r'"?(\w+)"?\s+\w+[^,]*?CHECK\s*\(\s*"?(\w+)"?\s+IN\s*\(([^)]*)\)\s*\)', ddl, re.I | re.S):
        vals = re.findall(r"'([^']*)'", m.group(3))
        if vals: vocab.setdefault(t, {})[m.group(2)] = vals
    for m in re.finditer(r"CHECK\s*\(\s*\"?(\w+)\"?\s+IN\s*\(([^)]*)\)", ddl, re.I | re.S):
        vals = re.findall(r"'([^']*)'", m.group(2))
        if vals: vocab.setdefault(t, {}).setdefault(m.group(1), vals)
res["check_vocab"] = vocab
# lifecycle flag columns
life = {}
for t in tables:
    cols = [c[1] for c in con.execute(f'pragma table_info("{t}")')]
    fl = [c for c in cols if re.search(r"(retired|revoked|resolved|superseded|closed|disposed)_(at|by|ref|session)|^status$|_status$|^disposition$|^state$|superseded_by", c)]
    if fl: life[t] = fl
res["lifecycle_cols"] = life
res["rows"] = rows
# unique indexes on judgment extraction table
uniq = []
for r in con.execute("select name, sql from sqlite_master where type='index' and sql like 'CREATE UNIQUE%' and tbl_name='source_value_extractions'"):
    uniq.append(r[0])
res["unique_on_source_value_extractions"] = uniq
# lens columns on tables
lens = {}
for t in tables:
    cols = [c[1] for c in con.execute(f'pragma table_info("{t}")')]
    ls = [c for c in cols if c in ("identity_code", "icf_code", "needs_code", "medical_code", "population_code")]
    if ls: lens[t] = ls
res["lens_columns"] = lens
res["population_named_tables"] = [t for t in tables if "population" in t]
res["tier_columns"] = {t: [c[1] for c in con.execute(f'pragma table_info("{t}")') if c[1] in ("tier", "evidence_type", "scope", "tier_basis")] for t in tables if any(c[1] in ("tier",) for c in con.execute(f'pragma table_info("{t}")'))}
# views: which stage tables they read; filter status?
vinfo = {}
for v, sql in views.items():
    refs = sorted({t for t in tables if re.search(rf'\b{re.escape(t)}\b', sql or "")})
    vinfo[v] = {"reads": refs, "stages": sorted({st(t) for t in refs}), "filters_status": bool(re.search(r"status|retired_at|revoked_at|superseded", sql or "", re.I)), "rows": None}
    try: vinfo[v]["rows"] = con.execute(f'select count(*) from "{v}"').fetchone()[0]
    except Exception as e: vinfo[v]["rows"] = f"ERR {e}"[:60]
res["views"] = vinfo
json.dump(res, open(out, "w"), indent=1, default=str)
print("user_version", uv, "tables", len(tables), "views", len(views), "| not in stage map:", res["in_schema_not_in_stage_map"], "| stale in stage map:", res["in_stage_map_not_in_schema"])
print("UNWRITABLE:", len(res["unwritable"])); [print("  ", u) for u in res["unwritable"]]
print("population-named tables:", res["population_named_tables"])
print("unique idx on source_value_extractions:", uniq)

# regenerate_derived.sh — regenerate every DB-derived output the CORRECT way, then verify.
#
# Lesson (2026-07-24): a dashboard was regenerated with `python3 tool.py > out.html`, which
# captured the tool's stdout STATUS LINE instead of its HTML — the tools write their own

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

echo "== Regenerating DB-derived outputs (tool writers, never stdout redirect) =="
python3 tools/pipeline_completeness.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Load every atoms-*.jsonl, classify each into a primitive type (HEURISTIC tag), write flat.jsonl + flat.tsv,
and produce candidate conflict pairs among ACTIVE atoms for human adjudication.
A candidate pair is NOT a conflict; it is a place to look. usage: flatten.py"""
import glob, json, re, itertools, collections, csv
atoms = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob("atoms-*.jsonl")):
    for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8"):
        if line.strip():
            a = json.loads(line); a["_file"] = f; atoms.append(a)
ids = collections.Counter(a["id"] for a in atoms)
dups = [i for i, n in ids.items() if n > 1]
PRIM = [  # (primitive, regex over subject+claim) -- first match wins; heuristic
    ("SPINE", r"\bstage(s)?\b.*\b(order|spine|seven|six|five)\b|\bspine\b|\bsevenstage\b"),
    ("STAGE-ASSIGN", r"\bis a (judgment|evidence|base)[- ]?(stage )?table\b|\bstage\b.*\btable\b|table is never a stage"),
    ("CARDINALITY", r"\b(1:N|N:1|1:1|one-to-many|many rows|fan-?(in|out)|cardinality)\b"),
    ("KEY-GRAIN", r"\bkeyed?\b|\bgrain\b|lens column|\bcheck\b.*lens|at least one|parameter_id|determination key"),
    ("POINTER-HOME", r"point, do not copy|second table|dual home|system of record|pointer|copy|duplicat|DOI column"),
    ("WRITE-PATH", r"migration|db\.py|\bverb\b|writ(e|er)|CLI|directly|canonical DB"),
    ("EVIDENCE-STATE", r"\bstated\b|provisional|pending|tier|marker|band|weak band|● |◐|○|regulatory stratum|convergence|independent root"),
    ("VOCAB-NAMING", r"\bname\b|vocabular|alias|enum|jurisdiction|substrate|population|lens|taxonom|term\b|parameter name|AX-"),
    ("RENDER", r"render|page|register|display|site|parts/"),
    ("GATE-AUDIT", r"\bcheck\b|\baudit\b|gate|EXAMINED|adversarial|attestation|DoD|preflight"),
    ("RESEARCH-CONDUCT", r"search|mining|retriev|locator|DOI|citation|source|candidate|admission|ERIC|scan|harvest|observ"),
    ("DOCTRINE", r"thinking tool|authority|mission|Co-1|advocacy|professional judgment|CRPD|prescription"),
    ("PRECEDENCE", r"supersede|outrank|precedence|ratif|owner ruling"),
    ("PROCESS", r"commit|PR\b|scratchpad|session|workflow|agent|branch|pull request|ensure-deps|suite"),
]
CAP = {"C1-mine-many-params": r"scan|harvest|mine|mining|any (and all )?(applicable )?parameter|across (multiple|any)|observ|every source|one source",
       "C2-grow-params": r"add-term|add-parameter|parameter (list|catalogue|registry|base)|vocabulary (is )?grow|mint|prepopulat|seed|catalogue",
       "C3-synth-across": r"synthes|convergence|compound|cross-(item|population|parameter)|conflict|divergen|connection",
       "C4-specify-render": r"specif|determination|render|page|figure for thought|register|assess_cell"}
def prim(a):
    t = f"{a['subject']} {a['claim']}"
    for p, rx in PRIM:
        if re.search(rx, t, re.I): return p
    return "OTHER"
def caps(a):
    t = f"{a['subject']} {a['claim']}"
    return [c for c, rx in CAP.items() if re.search(rx, t, re.I)]
